title: 'I can't believe it' - Lowry powers to record Irish Open win
description: Shane Lowry produces a frontrunning masterclass to cruise to a record 11-shot win at the Irish Open and end his four-year wait for an individual title in emphatic style.
fullText:
-23 S Lowry (Ire); -12 P Reed (US), J Niemann (Chi); -11 R Neergaard-Petersen (Den); -10 T McKibbin (NI), G De Leo (Ita)

Selected others: -9 A Fitzpatrick (Eng), J Skov Olesen (Den); -8 E Ferguson (Sco); -7 P Waring (Eng); -6 S Garcia (Spa), M Wallace (Eng), R MacIntyre (Sco); -4 J Rahm (Spa), D Law (Sco), R Fisher (Eng); -3 L Nolan (Ire); -1 R McIlroy (NI), +2 B Koepka (US).

Shane Lowry produced a frontrunning masterclass to clinch a record 11-shot win at the Irish Open and end his four-year wait for an individual title in emphatic style.

The 39-year-old Irishman, who entered the final round four strokes clear of Jacob Skov Olesen, carded a seven-under 63 to win his national open for the second time - 17 years after his first - amid joyous scenes at Trump International Golf Links in Doonbeg, County Clare.

Under the watchful gaze of visiting US President Donald Trump - who presented him with the trophy - and roared home by thousands of fans, Lowry mixed eight birdies and one bogey to canter to his first title since September 2022.

Having squandered chances to win in Dubai and Florida earlier this year, Lowry was a study in intensity and focus until the emotion poured out of him after he sunk a 29-foot birdie putt on the final green.

"This year has been quite difficult on the course for me," said the 2019 Open champion.

"I had a few chances to win. To come here this week and do this, I don't know, I just don't do things like half-measures."

Lowry shot 67-62-65-63 for a tournament record score of 257, while American Patrick Reed and Chile's Joaquin Niemann shared second place on 12 under.

Irish Open: Recap as Dominant Lowry cruises to 11-shot win at Doonbeg

Lowry - who posted a course-record 62 to seize control of the tournament on Friday - stumbled down the stretch earlier this year while chasing wins at the Dubai Invitational and Cognizant Classic in Florida.

He also collapsed to a seven-over 79 in the final round of the Masters having trailed eventual winner Rory McIlroy by just two shots entering the final day, which he highlighted as an especially difficult experience during his post-victory remarks at Doonbeg.

On Sunday, however, he never gave the chasing pack hope as he birdied four of his first eight holes to reach 20 under, with a holed 43-footer for a birdie two on the seventh undoubtedly the highlight.

While he stumbled momentarily with a bogey on nine, he bounced right back on the next and birdied 14 before sinking another monster putt on 15.

Having nearly chipped in for another unlikely birdie on 16, Lowry parred the next before drawing one last roar from the crowd when he poured in a 29-footer on the final hole.

"A lot of things have went right for me but this has been the most spectacular week," added Lowry, who savoured another win on home soil after watching Irish boxer Katie Taylor win her farewell fight at Dublin's Croke Park last week.

"It's just mad. I can't believe it. My mum was just standing there. I have my wife and my kids back in Florida.

"When things are not going well at this level, it's hard at home as well but my wife has been a huge support and my kids, I love them so much. I'm so happy for them.

"I can't wait to bring a trophy home. My daughter is always asking, 'when are you going to bring a trophy home?', so I'm going to bring a trophy home."

Denmark's Rasmus Neergaard-Petersen matched Lowry's 63 to finish fourth, while Northern Ireland's Tom McKibbin shot 67 to secure a top-five finish.

England's Alex Fitzpatrick (65) and Scotland's Ewen Ferguson (64) also finished strongly to seal top-10 finishes, while 2025 winner Rory McIlroy closed with a 67 to finish a disappointing week in a tie for 41st, 22 shots adrift of Lowry.

Reed's tie for second will also widen his lead over McIlroy at the top of the season-long Race to Dubai rankings.

However, six-time major winner McIlroy insisted he was reasonably satisfied with his game heading into the BMW PGA Championship at Wentworth, which begins on Thursday.

"I think overall, I've seen enough good stuff this week to give me encouragement going into next week, a golf course that I know well and a golf course that I've had success on," said McIlroy, who tumbled down the leaderboard with a 74 on Saturday.

"[It] obviously wasn't the week that I wanted but at the same time, I don't feel too far away, and I feel good about going into Wentworth next week."

title: Antonelli impressive and one of Colapinto's best weekends - driver ratings
description: BBC Radio 5 Live F1 commentator Harry Benjamin rates how the drivers performed during the Spanish Grand Prix.
fullText:
Kimi Antonelli won the Spanish Grand Prix at the new Madring circuit to extend his title advantage over Mercedes team-mate George Russell to 81 points.

Wolrd champion Lando Norris was leading the race from pole position but he lost out during the virtual safety car period and finished third, with Red Bull's Max Verstappen completing the podium in second place.

Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton was one of four retirements, after a brake failure ended his grand prix early on. The seven-time world champion has now lost ground on title leader Antonelli, but stays third in the standings.

Here are my ratings for how the drivers performed across the whole weekend in Madrid.

Quick throughout the weekend and missed pole by just 0.011 seconds, before being in exactly the right place to benefit from the virtual safety car. A couple of trips off the circuit early on stops it being faultless, but another impressive victory from Mercedes' championship leader.

Another excellent weekend from Red Bull's Verstappen. Qualified third, briefly fought for the lead on lap one and then did brilliantly to keep a faster Lando Norris behind him in the closing stages to secure second.

Probably deserved to win this one. Produced a sensational lap for pole, built a comfortable lead and looked in control until the virtual safety car fell at exactly the wrong moment before a slow pit stop compounded his misfortune.

Solid recovery after being narrowly beaten by team-mate Lewis Hamilton in qualifying. Ferrari rolled the dice by leaving him out and he led for a long time, but fourth was probably about the maximum once the hoped for safety car failed to arrive.

Started the weekend strongly but sixth in qualifying was disappointing compared with team-mate Antonelli on the front row. A tidy race brought fifth, but once again title-leading Antonelli had the upper hand.

Another very strong showing for Red Bull, in Isack Hadjar's continued absence. Reached Q3 and then led the midfield home in sixth, making good use of an opportunity that is becoming increasingly familiar, rather than simply being a one-off substitute appearance.

One of his best Formula 1 weekends. Put the Alpine into Q3 when team-mate Pierre Gasly could only manage 14th, and then produced a superbly controlled drive to seventh in the race, holding off Oscar Piastri in a much quicker McLaren late on.

A difficult weekend. Seven places behind team-mate Norris in qualifying was already disappointing before first-lap contact with Russell damaged his car, and eighth represented a poor return from a McLaren capable of winning the race.

A very good recovery after crashing heavily on Friday and missing much of final practice while the car was repaired. Still made Q3 and converted that into ninth place and another points finish.

Just missed Q3 but made sure Audi came away with something on Sunday. Beat team-mate Gabriel Bortoleto in qualifying and the race and grabbed the final point with another typically solid weekend.

Antonelli wins as Norris loses out under virtual safety car

How VSC cost Norris race win - and should F1 change the rules?

Haas had enough pace to threaten the lower end of the points but Ocon couldn't quite get there. Eleventh still represented a solid result and he comprehensively led the team's challenge after team-mate Oliver Bearman's difficult weekend.

A strange weekend after looking capable of reaching Q3 during practice. Qualified five places behind team-mate Colapinto and then finished five places behind him as well, which made this a rare weekend where the balance at Alpine swung heavily towards the other side of the garage.

Was right in the points battle for much of the race but ultimately slipped backwards to 13th. Not a disastrous weekend, although Audi team-mate Hulkenberg had the edge when it mattered.

Lost running with a power steering problem on Friday and never really recovered the momentum. Fifteenth in qualifying and 14th in the race was a long way from team-mate Lindblad's performance in the other Racing Bulls.

A difficult weekend for Williams at a circuit that didn't suit the car. Contact with the barrier cost him all of final practice, and he could only manage 15th on Sunday, although he did at least finish well clear of his team-mate Carlos Sainz.

The big crash in final practice effectively ruined his weekend. Haas couldn't repair the car for qualifying and a pit lane start left him with very little chance of recovering on a circuit where overtaking proved difficult.

A miserable home weekend but much of Sunday was outside his control. Sainz squeezed him into the wall early on and Aston Martin's power unit problems left him struggling badly thereafter.

His qualifying attempt was hurt when Sainz impeded him but Cadillac remained a long distance from the competitive midfield anyway. Made it to the finish but three laps down summed up the teams lack of pace.

A home weekend to forget. Knocked out in Q1, penalised for impeding Bottas, made contact with Tsunoda and was then penalised again for squeezing Alonso into the wall before eventually retiring.

At least had the upper hand over team-mate Bottas in qualifying but there wasn't much opportunity to build on it. His afternoon eventually ended with a suspected water-system problem.

Barely had a chance to get his weekend going properly. Power unit problems prevented him setting a qualifying time before brake trouble brought his race to an end and triggered the virtual safety car that ultimately decided the winner.

The final result hid a lot of good work. Recovered brilliantly from his crash in final practice to qualify fourth, and looked genuinely competitive at the start before a brake failure ended what could have been a podium challenge after only seven laps.

title: Joint-worst start since 1992 and fan protests - Man Utd's day to forget
description: Manchester United fans protested inside and outside Old Trafford before Sunday's derby, then saw their team lose to 10-man Manchester City
fullText:
Sir Jim Ratcliffe cannot have imagined it would be like this.

When Ratcliffe agreed on Christmas Eve 2023 to spend £1.25bn to buy a minority stake in Manchester United, his intention was to restore the ailing club to its past glories.

Sitting in the directors' box at Old Trafford watching United lose 1-0 to a Manchester City side reduced to 10 men midway through the first half was definitely not part of the plan.

Ratcliffe knew major decisions needed to be made in order to slash the club's losses. And he knew they were bound to be unpopular.

But nearly three years on, he presumably felt the green shoots of recovery would be starting to grow by now.

After all, the project chief executive Omar Berrada spoke to staff about in September 2024 was an aspiration to win the Premier League title in 2028. In other words, next season.

On the evidence of this 199th Manchester derby, United are a very long shot to achieve Berrada's target.

At this point, even pacifying the thousands of fans who protested against the club's ownership before the Old Trafford defeat by 10-man City looks beyond them.

United now have four points from their opening four games. It equals their worst start to a Premier League season since 1992-93. Last season under Ruben Amorim, they also had four points from four matches.

Was Haaland's winner a VAR error? Man Utd fury at 'injustice'

Haaland scores controversial winner for 10-man City at Man Utd

To be clear, United's fans have - to a greater or lesser degree - protested against the owners since the Glazer family landed £600m-worth of debt on to a previously debt-free club with their leveraged buy-out in 2005.

In their most recent accounts to 31 March, United had an overall debt of £1.3bn, including outstanding transfer fees.

Since then they have refinanced $425m (£314m) worth of bonds at a higher interest rate than they had been previously. They also took an additional $125m (£92.4m) but are yet to explain what the additional funds will be used for.

The club's current financial position will be revealed on 23 September when it publishes its full year accounts to 30 June 2026.

Ratcliffe's involvement promised to change the situation. Yet many fans argue that, if anything, things have got worse.

Ill feeling has spilled over since United launched a ticket-touting investigation in the summer.

Although they have admitted to underestimating the number of fans who shared their account details and toned down some of the threats around season ticket confiscation if supporters failed to respond as requested, United officials defended the investigation.

Last week, they revealed 685 fan accounts had been banned, with a further 464 either sanctioned or warned.

However, United added that "468 cases were resolved after supporters responded with the relevant information. No further action was taken, as the information provided satisfactorily explained the activity identified".

Many match-going fans felt the investigation was an attack on them and decided to use the City game to protest - inside and outside Old Trafford.

Huge numbers with flares gathered outside the ground, heeding a call from the 1958 Group, before making their way through the Munich tunnel under the stadium.

Inside, The Red Army group of fans opted not to bring in their usual banners - instead display a single banner above the players' tunnel stating: "The way you treat us is a disgrace."

It meant the only banners in the stadium were the ones the club had themselves put up.

"Unless our generational match-going support is given a real voice that is actually listened to, the little that remains of our fan culture will soon be gone forever," said The Red Army group in a statement.

"TRA aren't a protest group, we're an 'atmosphere' group but we've never shied away from making our position clear when we believe not doing so would be to the detriment of the interests of match-going supporters."

It was noticeable many songs were sung in direct protest against Ratcliffe, as well as the Glazers.

"We wanted the Glazers out and that will never change," said Steve Compton of the the 1958 Group.

"Ratcliffe came in and gave us a glimmer, but his idea of putting Manchester back in Man Utd couldn't be any further from the truth.

"The club have made many statements, but one thing they haven't done is actually apologise to anyone. We've had hundreds of messages directly - this has affected people's health.

"These are regular Joes, working-class people who are sent an email telling them their ticket's been suspended with no actual evidence. How do you defend something you don't know what you're defending against?"

BBC Sport has approached Manchester United for comment.

Foden sees red as Mainoo impresses - Manchester derby ratings

There were boos from the home fans at the final whistle, although it was not entirely clear whether the reaction was triggered by their team's performance or the officials over the controversial offside call that confirmed Erling Haaland's second-half winner should stand.

Since Berrada spoke to staff, United have delivered their worst starts in three decades. Many United supporters feel an overall transfer spend of £148m this summer was not enough after Carrick's mid-season arrival led to an improvement that secured a third-place finish.

"I definitely appreciate the supporters," said Carrick.

"We want to try everything to make them happy. They're everything for this football club. I never take them for granted. I speak about that quite a lot, and it means a lot to me.

"I'm feeling for them today on the back of losing the game. We haven't got as many points as we would have liked at this point, for sure. There's no getting away from that."

title: Two games, two defeats - are Olid's Man Utd in trouble?
description: Two games into the season under new manager Eva Olid, Manchester United look a shadow of the side from last season.
fullText:
Two shots for, with only one on target. Twenty-five efforts faced and five goals conceded.

Those numbers are enough to tell the story of Manchester United's humiliating 5-0 defeat by Chelsea in the Women's Super League (WSL) on Sunday.

A week after opening their season with a 2-1 defeat by big-spending London City Lionesses, United were completely overrun in Leigh on an afternoon that laid bare the gap between them and the WSL's elite.

It is difficult to believe that this team were competing with the same opponents for a place in Europe just a few months back, ultimately finishing nine points behind the Blues in fourth place under Marc Skinner.

But two games into the season under new manager Eva Olid, United look to have fallen further behind their rivals.

United have failed to win their opening two WSL games for the first time since their debut 2019-20 season, when they lost 1-0 to Arsenal and Manchester City.

But the manner of this loss, watched from the stands by the club's director of football operations Ameesh Manek, will be just as concerning for Olid as the accompanying statistics.

Of United's two shots, the first was a tame attempt from Elisabeth Terland 10 minutes in while the other - coming 72 minutes later from substitute Lea Schuller - was blocked at the edge of the box.

Sonia Bompastor's Chelsea, meanwhile, moved the ball with a speed and precision that United were unable to match up to.

"Chelsea are a good side and we knew we had to defend," Olid said.

"When you have the ball, you need to keep it longer. Don't lose the ball and create transitions. Keep it until we find the spaces to penetrate and create chances.

"They hurt us a lot in the wide areas too. We have to be better."

No WSL experience but who is new Man Utd boss Olid?

Have Man Utd lost faith in their women's team?

Olid promises 'brave' Man Utd with new-look style

Perhaps a poor start was to be expected after losing several key players in the summer and a move towards a sustainable model, focused on youth development.

Melvine Malard, who was their most productive player last season with 19 goal involvements, was sold to Chelsea.

Defender Millie Turner and midfielder Lisa Naalsund also left for promoted Birmingham City - with the trio part of the 2023-24 Women's FA Cup-winning squad.

New arrivals are still bedding in with Sweden winger Monica Jusu Bah, signed from BK Hacken, only having eight touches in 63 minutes and midfielder Rebeca Bernal picking up a yellow card on her debut off the bench.

Full-back Andrea Medina, who joined from Atletico Madrid, was their brightest spark but was distraught after she was forced off with an injury in the second half.

"We never enjoy losing football games and we never enjoy losing by five goals," striker Terland said.

"We all want to win and that is why we play football. We can't do anything about the result today, so we have to take the learning form it and move forward."

Olid had urged her players to be "brave" and have an "attacking mindset" this season.

The Spaniard guided Hearts to their first Scottish Women's Premier League title last campaign but arrived at United untested in the WSL and in Europe.

And questions will be raised about her appointment if the club fail to recover from this lacklustre start.

Replacing Skinner was never going to be a straightforward task.

The former manager often divided opinion among supporters during his five-year reign, but still led the club to a first major trophy with the FA Cup triumph, three other cup finals, two top-three finishes and the Women's Champions League quarter-finals last season.

His departure came after hints of frustrations over the lack of investment in the squad - just like his predecessor Casey Stoney who stepped down in 2021.

There is an argument Skinner overachieved, working with fewer resources than United's rivals.

In recent years, the club has been criticised for its training facilities, while owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe's comments about the women's team also drew ire.

Olid, who arrived with a remit to develop young players and build an attacking football identity, insisted perspective was needed after a winless start.

"It's what I said to the players - that it's just the beginning," she said.

"It's just two matches. It's not how you start but how you finish. Now we need them to learn from the mistakes and grow to go from down to high - that's our idea."

It is not going to get any easier for Olid, with her side visiting Emirates Stadium next week to take on Arsenal before facing West Ham.

Her side also have meetings with Liverpool and Manchester City next month.

"We are not going to stop," Olid said. "We will keep working hard and hope next week, we can feel that improvement."

After the crushing defeat, Terland was asked what it was like to play under the new United boss.

"It has been very new and exciting and she wants to play attacking football, she wants to keep the ball and find a fun way of playing football," the Norway international said.

"If we can get that to work, it will be a very fun way of playing football. It takes a lot of time to adapt as it is very different to what we have done before but if we continue to develop it will be fine."

Olid might be asking for patience but, if results do not improve, the coming weeks might test how much of it exists at United.

title: Dominant Kerr wins $150k with GB's first Ultimate title
description: Josh Kerr ends a sensational season by winning the Ultimate Championship 1500m title as the inaugural edition of athletics' new global event concludes.
fullText:
Josh Kerr ended a sensational season by being crowned Britain's first winner at the Ultimate Championship with a dominant 1500m victory - and earning $150,000 - as the inaugural edition of athletics' new global event concluded in Budapest.

Kerr smashed the 27-year mile world record at the London Diamond League and won Commonwealth Games gold in Glasgow this summer, after beginning an outstanding year by reclaiming the world indoor 3,000m title.

In the shape of his life, Kerr swept past American Yared Nuguse on the back straight in Hungary and would not be denied once he had made his move to the front, taking victory in three minutes 29.35 seconds.

"I am a major championship guy and I will always say that," Kerr, 28, told BBC Sport.

"From seven weeks ago in London, I went home, I chopped wood and carried water and I was ready to go again.

"Sometimes you have to come out of it to dig deeper and go further in life. Two weeks before [a race] I try to do something to get me out my routine and then I push myself for the last few weeks. If I didn't finish with a win, then that was on me."

The 2023 world champion did not qualify by right for the Ultimate Championship, which is reserved for reigning global champions, Diamond League winners and others based on world ranking.

He was instead awarded an exceptional invitation by World Athletics, alongside rival Jakob Ingebrigtsen - although the pair's eagerly-anticipated reunion did not transpire after the Norwegian withdrew following his 5,000m win on Friday.

Kerr was peerless as he seized the opportunity to put on one final show this season - and take his share of the biggest prize pot in the sport's history.

Over the past three nights, the world's top athletes competed for a new title and a total prize fund of $10m (£7.4m) at the innovative event, which World Athletics president Lord Coe hopes can play a key role in shaping the sport's future.

title: Twenty-five years in the waiting - Coventry's nightmare top-flight return
description: Coventry City's dream return to the Premier League is beginning to unravel after a fourth consecutive defeat - but can Frank Lampard turn it around?
fullText:
Coventry have waited 25 years for a return to the Premier League, but the reality of realising that dream is suddenly starting to look rather miserable.

Their campaign could not have started much worse with four successive defeats all without scoring a goal - the latest a 5-0 thrashing at home to Brighton - highlighting the brutality of the top flight.

The unwanted records are already beginning to pile up for Frank Lampard's side.

It is the club's worst start to a season since 1919-20 when they lost their opening nine matches in what was their first league campaign.

Their lack of goals means they are only the fifth side in English top-flight history to lose each of their opening four matches of the campaign while also failing to score at least once - after Derby Country (1899-1900), Stoke City (1906-07), Preston North End (1924-25) and Crystal Palace (2017-18).

Even though the West Midlands side had been dealt a tough start to life back in the big time, including fixtures at Arsenal and Manchester City, the manner in which they were thrashed on Sunday will raise alarm bells about what the rest of the season might have in store.

Coventry's performance last weekend against Manchester City appeared to be a step in the right direction.

The Sky Blues were unlucky not to come away with at least a point as they put goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma under real pressure with 12 shots and recorded an xG of 1.37.

Those signs of improvement continued in the first half against Brighton as they fired off 10 shots and created a handful of chances through Frank Onyeka and Jack Rudoni, while trailing by just one goal at the break.

But things began to unravel shortly after the break when some poor defending handed Brighton the opportunity to double their lead, before Taiwo Awoniyi was sent off for a flailing elbow two minutes later.

Coventry have now lost their last 46 Premier League matches when conceding first, a run that stretches back to March 1999.

"There's been some really poor defending from Coventry today," said former Manchester United captain Roy Keane on Sky Sports.

"You would think at 3-0 they would take the defeat and move on, but with some of the decision making today...they start looking like a Championship team.

"Frank has got to be really careful now that this team do not lose their belief."

Since the Premier League began in 1992, only one team (Southampton - 2012/13) has survived relegation after losing their opening four games of the campaign.

In the wider history of the English top flight, 10 of the 18 teams who have lost their first four matches of a season have been relegated (56%).

It is not the first time Lampard has been tasked with transforming the fortunes of Coventry.

When he was appointed as Mark Robins' successor in November 2024, the Sky Blues were 17th in the Championship, only two points above the relegation places.

Less than 18 months later, the 48-year-old was being hailed as a miracle worker after overseeing Coventry's dominant Championship campaign, which ended with the club's first promotion to the Premier League since 2001.

But his record in the top flight during his time at Chelsea and Everton was less impressive, with the former England international having won only four of his last 34 matches.

"The players gave everything until the end but it doesn't feel nice. We have to take some responsibility and understand they are the levels we need to raise to," Lampard told Sky Sports.

"We just continue to work. We are four games into the season when we have played the two most difficult fixtures [Arsenal and Manchester City away]. You always have to continue to work and the feeling is different in the Premier League.

"It is more pressure and a lot of players have not been near that. We're not feeling sorry for ourselves and they have to keep working and working. I've been in this situation many, many times."

title: Was Haaland's winner a VAR error? Man Utd fury at 'injustice'
description: Manchester City celebrate a remarkable derby win over Manchester United but questions remain over whether Erling Haaland's winning goal should have stood in a match fraught with controversy.
fullText:
As Manchester City celebrated a remarkable derby victory over Manchester United, there were questions as to whether Erling Haaland's winning goal should have stood in a match fraught with controversy.

Striker Haaland found the net on 60 minutes at Old Trafford, turning home at the back post from Josko Gvardiol's cross before it was disallowed on the field for offside.

Following intervention from the video assistant referee, the goal was awarded - the Norwegian ruled to have been played onside by Patrick Dorgu's boot.

But there was debate as to whether the offside Enzo Fernandez, diving at the ball in a more central position than Haaland, was interfering with play.

United defender Lisandro Martinez said it was an "injustice" while boss Michael Carrick said he was "confused" by the decision.

The goal came after City had gone down to 10 men in the first half when Phil Foden was shown a straight red card for kicking out at United captain Bruno Fernandes.

Foden was dismissed by referee Michael Oliver on 23 minutes after kicking the midriff of Fernandes while he was on the turf.

Should Haaland's goal have stood? Should Foden have been sent off? And was Fernandes fortunate to avoid a red card himself?

When Haaland's goal was ruled out as offside on the field, few questioned the decision as the City striker looked to have drifted beyond United's defensive line.

The lines drawn by the VAR showed Haaland to be onside thanks to Dorgu's boot. But it was the positioning and involvement of Fernandez that left many pundits astounded and unsure if it was a legitimate goal.

Gvardiol's cross took a slight deflection off the boot of Dorgu before finding its way to Haaland at the back post, while Fernandez was clearly attempting a diving header in the middle of the six-yard box but he did not touch the ball.

Fernandez appeared to be in an offside position, ahead of Dorgu's boot, but VAR deemed it to be a legitimate goal as he did not touch the ball while United defender Martinez was also closing in.

The Premier League Match Centre said on X: "VAR checked the referee's call of no goal for offside - and determined that Haaland was in an onside position and recommended that the goal was awarded.

"The VAR also deemed that while in an offside position, Fernandez didn't play the ball."

Dale Johnson, BBC Sport football issues correspondent

The curiosity about this incident is that the goal was initially disallowed for the wrong reason. Haaland was flagged offside when he shouldn't have been.

But as it turned out, the goal should have been ruled out because Fernandez was offside.

There is one key part of the offside law which applies to Fernandez here. A player is offside if they are:

"Clearly attempting to play a ball which is close when this action impacts on an opponent."

Both parts of that clause must be met. It is possible for a player in an offside position to attempt to play a ball and not commit an offence – there must be impact on an opponent too.

As the ball came in, Fernandez threw himself to try to head it, with Martinez directly behind him.

Video assistant referee Matt Donohue should ask himself if Fernandez's action would have influenced Martinez.

In other words: If Fernandez had not jumped for the attempted header, would Martinez have made a different decision over playing the ball?

If the ball had been out of reach for Fernandez, or for Martinez, then there is an argument to give the goal.

And also: There would have been no offside had Fernandez made no attempt to play the ball.

But he did. And as it went just a yard in front of Martinez too, it is very difficult to argue Fernandez did not commit an offside offence.

There is also an argument that the actions of Fernandez influence the positioning of goalkeeper Senne Lammens.

However, the goal was originally ruled out for offside against Haaland - which was incorrect. So that decision had to be overturned.

And then, the VAR should have sent referee Michael Oliver to the monitor for the subjective offence by Fernandez.

It would have created the odd situation where a disallowed goal was reviewed to remain ruled out - but this is what should have happened.

It was a clear offside offence by Fernandez and will go down as a VAR mistake.

With Haaland's goal settling the match, United were unsurprisingly disappointed by the decision.

"I think it was offside," said Martinez. "And what I can't understand is the rules. I want to be calm now, I want to control myself.

"It's so hard because you lose a derby, you lose three points at home, and every season they're [referees] coming to our club, they explain for one hour the rules, and they look so confident with that, and then after [there are] five or six people doing these kind of mistakes in the Premier League - it's unacceptable.

"It's the best league in the world, you have the best teams in the world, the best players in the world, and now we have to go home with this injustice."

United boss Carrick also expressed his confusion.

"We put things in place in the game now, we have people in offices with all the screens for this decision," he said.

"It's more worrying about if that's the interpretation of football now. If that's the interpretation of not interfering in the game now, that's really worrying for me. It's a staggering explanation.

"The decision isn't going to change the season, but it's had a major impact on the game."

Wayne Rooney, part of the BBC's MOTD2 team, said: "Surely it's offside. Martinez is impacted by Fernandez's movement, and he is offside."

Gary Neville said on Sky Sports: "I think we'll see some sort of apology from the referee's association, there's no doubt Fernandez is playing that ball and is trying to put off Martinez. I think it's one they'll recognising they got wrong."

Micah Richards added: "I think it's been a bad day for referees. They got the Foden decision wrong and the Fernandez decision wrong. I think they got it so wrong but I don't think it takes anything away from City's performance."

Meanwhile, City boss Maresca said: "I think it was onside clearly so it's good."

The goal came after a first half laced with controversy, with Foden shown a straight red for kicking out at midfielder Fernandes.

City midfielder Foden picked up the ball wide on the right-hand side in his own half and was closed down by Fernandes, who tripped him.

Foden then kicked out at the body of the Portuguese midfielder while on the ground and was shown a straight red card by the referee.

Replays showed that Fernandes kicked Foden in the back first, before the England international retaliated.

The incident was checked by the VAR, who confirmed the on-field decision; Fernandes was not shown a card.

Pundits were divided on whether Foden should have seen red and whether Fernandes was the man at fault.

Former Manchester United forward Rooney did not believe it was a red, saying "it was more of a flick or a gesture, than a kick out".

Neville said he was "surprised" Fernandes did not receive a booking for his role while Roy Keane said the fault lay with the Portuguese midfielder.

"Foden gets up and reacts obviously, so he's sent off," he said. "Fernandes catches him and gives him a little kick. I guess it's classed as violent. But Fernandes is the one who is violent here, I don't think Foden should have a red card."

Dale Johnson, BBC Sport's issues correspondent, said: "The referee and VAR would have to deem it violent conduct rather than just petulance from Fernandes.

"The guidance changed some years ago to factor that in, so David Beckham's kick on Diego Simeone in the 1998 World Cup would not result in a sending off today.

"It looked to me like there was little to no contact from Fernandes, and if there was it was limited force and wasn't followed through.

"So Bruno's act would be seen as a yellow card offence, which the VAR obviously can't get involved in."

title: 'Finally got our points' - Hull and Woad shine in European Solheim win
description: Charley Hull gets the ball rolling as Europe's big guns finally came to the fore in Sunday's singles as they wrestled the Solheim Cup back from the United States with a 15½-12½ victory at Bernardus Golf Club in the Netherlands.
fullText:
Charley Hull got the ball rolling as Europe's big names finally came to the fore in Sunday's singles as they wrestled the Solheim Cup back from the USA with a 15-13 victory in the Netherlands.

Hull, who had garnered just half a point across the first two days in an unprofitable partnership with fellow Englishwoman Lottie Woad, led Europe out again on Sunday and claimed a 3&2 win over American livewire Megan Khang.

It delivered an immediate boost to Anna Nordqvist's team in the singles format that they have been unbeaten in since their last home defeat in 2015.

Woad, who alongside Hull is ranked among the top 10 players in the world, also delivered, with her 2&1 win over fellow debutant Auston Kim sparking wild celebrations on the 17th green at Bernardus Golf Club.

With Carlota Ciganda three holes up heading on to the 16th, it assured the hosts of reaching the 14½-point tally required to triumph in the biggest team competition in women's golf.

"It was the no-brainer to put Charley first," said Nordqvist.

"We saw the stats and Charley and Lottie were actually top-four players that made the most birdies for the week. They just played really tough matches.

"People don't understand how good all these players are and how good the golf has been in the past three days.

"So Charley was a no-brainer, and then finishing strong with Carlota. As we know, she's done it in the past."

Any question marks over Nordqvist's captaincy had revolved around repeatedly pairing her two star English players together over the first two days.

And Hull was one of the first on the scene to congratulate Woad, with the quip, "finally got our points didn't we Lottie".

Veteran Ciganda officially carrying her side over the winning line by beating Jennifer Kupcho could not have been more fitting as she became just the second player to secure the decisive point twice - having done so in 2023 - joining Catriona Matthew who did the same for Europe in both 2003 and 2013.

On Saturday evening Kupcho had hushed the crowd and yelled "vamos" as she drained a 91-foot putt on the 17th and then knocked in a 30-footer on the 18th green to steal a point from the Spaniard in the fourballs.

It felt like a moment that had turned the momentum of the match towards Angela Stanford's team but fewer then 24 hours later, Kupcho and her US team-mates had little to cheer with all the euphoria draped around those wearing blue and yellow.

"I was really happy to see that I was playing against Kupcho," said Ciganda. "She's a fighter, I'm a fighter, and what she did was amazing on 17 and 18.

"But [on Sunday] I knew she had no chance. I was like, I want to kill you," joked the Spaniard.

Having started the day level at 8-8, Europe's quartet of rookies deserve huge credit.

Having impressed in the foursomes and fourballs, Spain's Julia Lopez Ramirez and France's Nastasia Nadaud once again demonstrated their suitability for the biggest of stages.

Lopez Ramirez defeated Yealimi Noh 3&2, while Nadaud always looked in control against Andrea Lee to win by the same scoreline.

Mimi Rhodes, who had partnered Nadaud to two victories, was only downed by a superb performance from world number one Nelly Korda, while Lauren Coughlin, Lindy Duncan, Alison Lee were the only others to put intermittent splashes of red on Sunday's scoreboard.

Coughlin, who had already earned two-and-a-half points this week, ended Leona Maguire's unbeaten singles record.

Duncan beat Maja Stark, while Alison Lee came from four holes down to complete the biggest singles comeback in the history of the Solheim Cup, with a 1UP success over Esther Henseleit.

But it was simply not enough for the visitors, whose wait for a first win on European soil since 2015 continues.

"The Europeans played great today, and that's the way it goes," said Stanford.

"Their backs were against the wall, they had nothing to lose, and that's exactly what they did, they came out and played well."

As the US team returned to their team hotel on Saturday, a picture was posted on social media of them celebrating Kupcho's heroics on the 17th and 18th greens with a crate of beer.

Those scenes will have certainly inspired Europe on Sunday and the home team managed the wet early conditions perfectly as the US toiled on the greens.

"When we showed up in July here, they were faster. And I don't think it had anything to do with the rain either," said Stanford when asked about the speed of the greens.

"It's my responsibility to get the team ready. This is the one thing I am kicking myself [over] is that I just didn't keep pushing. We got to figure out how to hit our putts a little bit harder, which is really difficult, to change the way you putt.

"So I'm a little frustrated with myself that I didn't drive that point home. We don't play on greens this slow usually,

"I don't think we played bad. I think we just didn't make enough putts. If you listen to everything I've ever said, Europeans always putt better.

"I don't know why. I still don't know why. I mean, I have a good idea, but I'm not going to say it right now. Apparently I didn't get to know the superintendent as well as I should have."

title: How virtual safety car cost Norris win - and should F1 change rules?
description: Lando Norris says he was "insanely unlucky" to lose what seemed like a certain win in the Spanish Grand Prix because of the timing of a virtual safety car.
fullText:
Lando Norris says he was "insanely unlucky" to lose what seemed like a certain win in the Spanish Grand Prix because of the timing of a virtual safety car.

McLaren's Norris was leading comfortably when the VSC was called, seconds after he had passed the pit lane entry.

That allowed Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli and Red Bull's Max Verstappen to pit under the VSC, saving time, while the caution period ended before Norris could make it around to the pits again.

Of the VSC, Norris said: "It is a rule that should not define a whole race."

"I was the only one on the whole grid that didn't get the chance to do the pit stop," he said. "That's just unfortunate.

"There's been plenty of times where I've gained from it in the past and times where I've lost from it, and it's racing, but never when fighting for a win.

"So, it's probably one of the first times a win has been lost simply because of it."

After taking pole position with a lap his team principal Andrea Stella described as "a masterpiece", Norris was leading Antonelli by more than six seconds after 13 laps in Madrid.

He had just passed the pit entry at the end of lap 14 when a VSC was called because Lance Stroll's Aston Martin had stopped in the run-off area at Turn 20, while Antonelli and Verstappen were far enough behind to pit.

The VSC, which controls all cars to a specified maximum speed, then ended shortly before Norris completed the next lap, at the end of which he pitted.

Because a stop under the VSC costs 11 seconds less race time than one under green-flag conditions, Norris lost sufficient time that Antonelli and Verstappen were able to pass him.

Norris lost a further five seconds because of problems with his two right-hand side tyres at the stop and emerged from the pits more than 15 seconds behind Antonelli and more than nine adrift of Verstappen.

He caught the Red Bull before the end of the race but as overtaking was virtually impossible on the new Madring street circuit, he was stuck in third place.

Race-winner Antonelli, who extended his championship lead to 81 points, acknowledged Norris' bad fortune. "If I have to be realistic and honest, today we didn't deserve to win," he said. "Lando deserved to win, and so I think our result was probably P2 or even P3."

Antonelli wins as Norris loses out under virtual safety car

Antonelli impressive and one of Colapinto's best weekends - driver ratings

The VSC is a system by which the cars are forced to drive to a specified lap-time delta while a hazard on track is cleared.

It is used in certain circumstances in favour of deploying the actual safety car, usually when the hazard can be cleared relatively quickly, because it interferes less with the race and minimises the time lost under caution.

A physical safety car involves a modified high-performance road car entering the track and having the field line up behind it.

The various protocols around its operation mean a safety-car period usually goes on for several laps, while in this case the VSC was in operation for less than a single lap.

The short duration of the VSC in this case was exactly why Norris was railing against the situation.

Every other driver in the field had the opportunity to decide whether to pit or not - the only driver not given that option was Norris.

The pit lane entry is before the final corner at the Madring, and Norris was in the last corner when it was called.

The VSC ended when Norris was in Turn 21, the corner before the pit entry, on lap 15. Antonelli, having stopped, was behind him in Turn 19.

On most circuits, Norris would have had a chance to pass Verstappen and perhaps even do the same to Antonelli before the end, given his pace advantage on the day, but as Antonelli put it: "In the race, you're just stuck behind."

Norris was withering in his criticism of the track layout, saying: "I don't know how someone looks at this design and goes, 'Mint.'" But he did say there was "a lot of opportunity" to improve it for next year.

After the race, one question asked of McLaren was whether pitting on the following lap was the best idea, or should Norris have stayed out?

Norris said: "I had to come in at the end of the lap because it was the only chance.

"It was still effectively some pit loss, (but) the fact that everyone's kind of on colder tyres and you're still minimising the pit loss.

"The medium tyre (on which Norris had started the race) was destroyed and the hard tyre (to which Antonelli and Verstappen switched) was amazing.

"But the pace was very, very strong and on the hard tyre... I know they were stuck (behind Ferrari's Charles Leclerc, who stayed out under the VSC), we caught up 13, 14 seconds or more, almost. So, plenty of positives. A day full of positives, just one thing let it all down."

McLaren team principal Andrea Stella said: "We considered staying out, but you have to accept the fact that now you are on relatively used medium tyres. And the people behind you will be on new hard. So you're never going to open a gap on people on new hard."

The other question was whether McLaren would have been wise to anticipate that the race director would call the VSC and pit Norris before it was deployed.

McLaren team principal Andrea Stella said: "In hindsight, that would have been a good idea."

But he pointed out that, in the moment, it would have come with risks. The long pit lane at the Madring - the longest on the calendar - meant a pit stop cost a lot of time.

Stella said: "I would have to review with my engineers, see whether it was kind of obvious that it would end up in a virtual safety car. Therefore, you try to anticipate or not.

"Here, the problem is that you need to be extremely careful, because it's 27 seconds if you don't pit under a virtual safety car.

"So if you get it wrong, it would be extremely penalising. From the lead, you pit unnecessarily, and now you have lost the victory.

"So a good rule is to respond to what is a fact, to what is the real condition of the circuit.

"But we will definitely take a look as to whether in these conditions it was just simply, you know, obvious that he would end up in a virtual safety car. I cannot answer at the moment."

VSCs and safety cars are commonplace in F1 and they always afford drivers and teams the chance to gain or lose depending on the decisions they make when they occur.

Norris took his maiden victory in Miami in 2024 with the help of a safety car - he had delayed his stop and was able to make it under caution when race leader Verstappen had already stopped, and jumped into the lead.

And in Barcelona this year, Lewis Hamilton's maiden Ferrari victory was helped by a VSC that gave him a cheap pit stop on a different tyre strategy from rivals Mercedes.

However, this is the only example many could remember of a race leader losing a race in this fashion by being the only driver not to be able to choose whether to pit under a VSC or safety car.

After the race, Norris and Verstappen said this kind of scenario had been discussed by drivers many times with governing body the FIA.

"I think there's always probably some cons to doing it, but it's tough," Norris said.

"I've won from it in the past, I've lost from it in the past. Over the course of a season, it's hard to know if it's a good thing or a bad thing.

"It probably equals out over time. Of course, it just hurts more, the fact that I lose a win. You know, there's literally nothing I could do as a driver today to do a better job."

Verstappen said: "We'll probably talk about it in the next briefing and see if there is anything that can be done."

Stella added: "Perhaps there's a wider reflection that the Formula 1 community should apply as to whether you keep things like they are or you introduce ways of maintaining more fairness.

"Offering the personal opinion. I'm puzzled myself as to what's right.

"Is it correct to give enough duration such that everyone will have been subject to the same track conditions? So, for instance, the virtual safety car lasts at least one full lap? Or you just keep it in the hands of the gods, and sometimes you are lucky, sometimes you are not. I'm not sure myself.

"But in general, there's the right place to have this sort of conversation, which is the Strategy Advisory Committee (SAC). And this is a topic that may be added to the agenda and discussed over there.

"But if there is to be a change, it will have to be a change that goes through the SAC, then the F1 Commission, and then we'll have to go at some stage to the sporting regulations.

"But I would envisage that this is a relatively lengthy process, unless there's a big push from F1, from the institutions, FIA or F1, to say, like, 'we need to make this different'."

title: McInnes delivers togetherness & intensity in Old Firm gobsmacker
description: BBC Scotland's chief sportswriter Tom English analyses Rangers' convincing Old Firm victory over Celtic at Ibrox.
fullText:
Fifty-five minutes into this Rangers romp at Ibrox, Martin O'Neill and Shaun Maloney stood beside each other in the Celtic technical area, chin-stroking, head-scratching, pointing, waving, drowning.

To them, in this moment, this Premier Sports Cup quarter-final must have felt like a surreal and nightmarish occasion - and it was only 1-0 at the time. Rangers had really only started to wreak their havoc.

Such was Rangers' dominance, their complete owning of their visitors in every conceivable category, the Celtic managerial brains trust seemed just as lost as every one of their players on the field.

Man for man, Rangers won every battle, not for 45 minutes but for the full ninety.

Rangers overwhelm meek Celtic to clinch semi-final spot

No away fans, of course. Not that that had anything to do with it. Being locked out of Ibrox might have seemed like a curse to Celtic folk. In the end, it must have felt like the greatest blessing.

In his early months in the job, Derek McInnes has been looking for a marquee performance. Now he has it. He was looking for a formation that worked and personnel that were big enough and bold enough to execute it and he got that, too. This was 3-0 going on more. Plenty more.

The simplicity of their progression to the semi-final was a touch surreal. Neither of these were in particularly good form coming into this. They were both winning, yes, but they haven't been all that convincing.

This season, in their last eight domestic features combined - all won, in fairness - there was only a goal in it at the end in seven of them. Both sides had got themselves into a cycle of missed chances and, at times, uncomfortable days.

So the smart money was on a tight contest. Extra-time, maybe. Penalties? You wouldn't have ruled that out either. O'Neill is such a winning machine that many would have expected Celtic to find a way, somehow. So much for that.

Few Old Firm games surprise you anymore, but this one was a gobsmacker.

Rangers had all the intensity and all the togetherness. They had six players making their Old Firm debut from the start but if inexperience can be a challenge in this fixture then it was a challenge they met with gusto.

McInnes and his driven and vastly superior players neutralised Celtic, shut them down, rendered them impotent. Celtic captain Callum McGregor lords it over days like this, but the supreme central midfielder was Dan Neil, not just in his outstanding goals but in the control and the leadership he exerted.

With Nico Raskin beside him it was a no-contest in the middle of the pitch. James Penrice did a power of really good work in there, too.

Camilo Duran, playing wide again instead of through the middle, has been one of the players of the season so far, but he hardly existed, totally bossed by Olwethu Makhanya - calm in the maelstrom, classy in nearly everything he did.

Kasper Hogh needed a goal having scored in just one game in six - a hat-trick, albeit - but the record signing spent much of his day in Emmanuel Fernandez's pocket. He had no service and no sniff.

Where did this come from? Lord knows, but it makes life very interesting now, not just in the destination of the League Cup - Rangers will be massive favourites against Aberdeen in their semi-final - but in the race for the league title.

McInnes might have hit on something substantial. The big task, of course, is to repeat that energy, that belief, that ruthlessness.

You expected Celtic to stir and make a game of it, but they were never allowed to, in part because of their own awful shortcomings with the ball and in other part because Rangers didn't allow them to settle. They hunted them down, right from the opening minutes.

A mood, of sorts, was set as early as the fourth minute when Sam Johnstone, Celtic's jumpy new goalkeeper, passed a clearance straight to Kevin Kelsy, who slashed it wide.

Johnstone had been harried by Rangers' press, a big theme of the day. For Kelsy, it was a great chance to strike early, but if he failed then he made amends later on.

Kelsy is only in the door, but he looks to have personality and desire. He was playing with Ryan Naderi, an oft-criticised striker, a player you hear constantly is not Rangers class. Naderi was one of the totems of the day, a work rate that never stopped, a constant menace in hunting and gathering. Naderi might have changed a few Rangers minds on Sunday.

The opener was a microcosm; Naderi robbing Cameron Carter-Vickers, Kelsy then picking out Neil for a sumptuous finish. Rangers were physically and creatively on top, but there's always a feeling that one goal needed to become two to halt Celtic's assumed purple patch, a response that never came.

That was the bizarre thing. Total authority for an entire game is a rare enough thing in this contest. Usually there's a spell when the team that's ahead has to weather some kind of storm. Celtic couldn't throw a bucket of water in Rangers' direction not to mind a tempest. When McInnes' side made it two it was only what they deserved.

Penrice put in the cross, Naderi flicked it on and Kelsy banged in the volley. Neil's second and Rangers' third was a peach, a sign of confident uninhibited players enjoying themselves. The smallest of mercies for Celtic was that it stayed at three.

The second part of this drama comes on Sunday, a league game that could not have been better set up had Eddie Hearn been involved in the promotion. Rangers looking to lay down another marker going to Celtic's home, full of 60,000 folk baying for revenge. Given some of the vile songs that were directed at O'Neill at Ibrox then McInnes is in for some treatment. Sadly, he's heard it all over before, as has O'Neill.

McInnes was measured in the aftermath, more low-key than you might have expected and there was sense in that. This was one game and he knew it. They won nothing on the back of it and he knew that, too.

Apart from, that is, precious momentum and self-belief and the knowledge of what their standard can be when they get it right. And on Sunday, they got it spectacularly right.

title: Syracuse football: Orange open as big underdog to Pitt
description: This time, I don’t think the odds are going to change who’s favored
fullText:
Thursday night road games at Pitt usually mean that the Sickos Committee will be pulling up with the lawn chairs and popcorn.

That will most certainly be the case as the Syracuse Orange travel to Acrisure Stadium (the artist formerly known as Heinz Field) to take on the Pittsburgh Panthers. The early opening odds, according to Fanduel, have Syracuse as a +9.5 point underdog. The Orange opened as a +1.5 underdog to Cal as well before the line shifted quickly into Syracuse's favor.

Syracuse needs a rebound win in the worst way possible after losing to Cal 21-18, a game the Orange probably should have won. Three interceptions from Steve Angeli and 15 penalties called on Syracuse dug the Orange grave at the JMA Wireless Dome on Saturday. Syracuse enters week three with an 1-1 record.

Pitt enters the game after the Panthers defense held strong against UCF on a rainy Saturday in the Steel City. UCF only had 206 yards of total offense as the Panthers won 12-7. Pitt is 2-0 on the season and is playing its third straight game at home to start the season. The Panthers will play one more home game next week before hitting the road for the first time in October to play Virginia Tech.

Thursday's game will be the first ACC contest this season for Pitt. The recent series history has not been kind to Syracuse. The Orange are 4-20 in the last 24 matchups against Pitt, with two straight losses. The last Syracuse victory came in 2023 at Yankee Stadium, which was the fabled Dan Villari game where he rushed for 154 yards.

The last time that Syracuse defeated Pitt in Pittsburgh was in 2001. That day, the Orange defense caused five turnovers and some guy name Troy Nunes threw a touchdown pass as Syracuse won 42-10. The Orange have lost 11 straight games to the Panthers in Pittsburgh.

Kickoff for Thursday's game is at 7:30 pm ET. The game will be aired on ESPN.

title: Rangers 3-0 Celtic – “On the day, just second best,” Martin O’Neill
description: Martin O’Neill spoke to the media at Ibrox this afternoon after Celtic exited the Premier Sports Cup at the quarter finals stage following a 3-0 mauling from the Rangers…13th September 2026; Ibrox...
fullText:
13th September 2026; Ibrox, Scottish League Cup Football, Rangers versus Celtic; Dan Neil of Rangers shoots and scores in the 22nd minute to make it 1-0. Photo Vagelis Georgariou

The Celtic performance was absolutely pathetic with only young Colby Donovan worthy of a passmark. Here's everything that a shell-shocked Celtic manager had to say about today's shambolic Celtic performance….

Q: Martin, what went wrong for your team today?

Martin O'Neill: "We were well beaten in the end. I thought the first half we didn't capitalise, we had a couple of really decent chances when we'd broken their press. But on the day, just second best."

13th September 2026; Ibrox. Scottish League Cup Football, Rangers versus Celtic; Rangers fans display. Photo Vagelis Georgariou

Q: What would you put that down to, Martin?

Martin O'Neill: "I think there has to be a realisation of how big this game is. It's so important to the fans, so important to everybody. It's still one of the great fixtures, as mentioned, in European football, if not the world. And people have got to know that. That's the point. We'll have to try and learn from it. We play next Sunday, we've got a midweek game. But really we have to. I think, hopefully, it's a wake-up call. I have to look at myself for a start, then I look at the team. We were second best."

Martin O'Neill at Ibrox. Premier Sports Cup quarter final. 13 September 2026. Photo Vagelis Georgariou

Q: Did that surprise you, Martin? You said it was a wake-up call.

Martin O'Neill:  "I think it is. You can go on, you can win some games, which we've been doing domestically and it's been fine. We've found a way to win a couple of matches which were difficult for us. We were beaten today. Did Rangers surprise me? No. I think they're strong. I think they're physically strong. So it'll be a big test for us next Sunday again, in every aspect."

Q: Martin, you said that Rangers didn't surprise you in terms of their commitment and effort levels, but were you surprised that they went with three at the back? Or do you think it was difficult for Celtic to deal with that?

Martin O'Neill:  "Not necessarily. I think you have to be able to deal with it. You deal with any sort of permutation that the opposition put in front of you. That's their prerogative, to do exactly that. I'm not so sure it's always to do with systems. Sometimes it is, sometimes it isn't. But if you do misplace a lot of passes, when you have comfortable possession, I don't think that's got to do with the systems, myself. I think, we did misplace a lot of passes today when we were comfortable and choosing the wrong option when we were on the counter-attack."

13th September 2026; Ibrox; Scottish League Cup Football, Rangers versus Celtic; Camilo Duran of Celtic. Photo Vagelis Georgariou

Q: Is that why you were unable to create such few opportunities?

Martin O'Neill:  "That's true. We didn't do. That's a bit of a surprise to me. The one thing that I felt, and I think I've been saying to you for weeks, certainly domestically, we look as if we can create. So it didn't materialise today. So we have to try and find out the reasons why. Just at this minute, I'm naturally disappointed, really disappointed about it. But we've got to gather ourselves together because the games are coming thick and fast for us."

Q: Martin, you made one change at the break. Were you tempted to make more, especially a couple of boys on yellow cards?

Martin O'Neill: "It could have changed. Me personally, I think young Colby has come out of this with great credit. I think he's an absolute warrior. Sometimes we misplace passes, but he's got a big heart. I think we can all learn from that. And because of the size of his heart, he was booked in the first half, but he kept going right to the end. He was booked against St Mirren after about eight or nine minutes, still kept going. In terms of heart and desire, he's been a big plus for us."

Olwethu Makhanya of Rangers is challenged by Benjamin Nygren of Celtic during the Premier Sports Cup Quarter Final match between Rangers and Celtic at Ibrox Stadium on September 13, 2026. (Photo by Ian MacNicol/Getty Images)

Q: Martin, obviously there are no away fans on the ground today. Did that play any part? Do you think maybe some of your team are overawed by the occasion?

Martin O'Neill: "Well, a lot of boys have, you know, Kieran Tierney and Callum, people like this here and James Forrest, they've all won here when there's been big crowds. And I think they've won. Was there anybody here when Covid set in? No? So they've played here before, so that I don't know. But certainly for some of the younger and the newer lads, it's an experience that I don't think they'll forget."

13th September 2026; Ibrox, Scottish League Cup, Rangers versus Celtic; Sam Johnstone of Celtic comes off the team bus. Photo Vagelis Georgariou

Q: Martin, Sam Johnstone wasn't the only Celtic player that found it difficult today but why did you opt for him ?

Martin O'Neill: "I want people to experience these games, because what other way am I going to learn about what people can or cannot do? What I don't want to do is just put people in so that I can learn something from it. The main object is obviously to try and win, and it's a fine balancing act from me.'

Q: Martin, is it a bad day at the office, or are you more concerned about the structural problems with the team at the moment?

Martin O'Neill: "Structural in what sense?

Q: Off the ball, losing possession?

Martin O'Neill: "Yes, I absolutely agree with you. I think we can do much, much better than that. I think we can get the ball back a bit more quickly than we certainly did today, and start getting back to dominating. So we'll see what next Sunday brings. In normal circumstances, I wouldn't mind just a full week to look at a few things and maybe work on a couple of things. But yes, we had players today who were below par, and well below par, and that's not a great mix."

13th September 2026; Ibrox, Scottish League Cup Football, Rangers versus Celtic; Benjamin Nygren of Celtic and Sebastian Tounekti of Celtic. Photo Vagelis Georgariou

Q: What was behind the decision to start with Sebastian Tounekti on the left? What was your thinking there?

Martin O'Neill: "Young Hassan had an overnight problem, and he didn't get much sleep in all honesty, so it was just a matter of not starting him because of that. That's the reason, really."

Q: Do you expect a bit more from your new arrivals in some of this kind of game? Is that a bit of a culture shock?

Martin O'Neill: "I hope it is. I hope it is, absolutely. I'm sure it will be. It was a culture shock for me 26 years ago when I came here, we got smashed 5-1."

Martin O'Neill, Manager of Celtic, arrives at the stadium before the Premier Sports Cup Quarter Final match between Rangers and Celtic at Ibrox Stadium on September 13, 2026. (Photo by Ian MacNicol/Getty Images)

Q: Martin, are you happy your next domestic fixture is against Rangers?

Martin O'Neill: "That would be good, yes. I'm looking forward to that I'm looking forward to our crowd making the same sort of noise as the Ibrox crowd made today."

title: “Lost for words” – Former Liverpool star slams performance against Fulham
description: Liverpool Held by Fulham as Anfield Frustration Grows for Andoni IraolaLiverpool are already six points behind Arsenal. Four league games in, that is not a crisis, but it is a fact. Facts matter. So d...
fullText:
Liverpool are already six points behind Arsenal. Four league games in, that is not a crisis, but it is a fact. Facts matter. So does context. And the context is simple, Liverpool have yet to win a Premier League home game under Andoni Iraola, and draws against Nottingham Forest and Fulham at Anfield are not the standard expected here.

This is a team in transition. Arne Slot is gone, Iraola is in, and a summer of change has left Liverpool short of the rhythm and certainty needed to keep pace at the top. That explains some of it. It does not excuse all of it.

Liverpool remain unbeaten, which sounds reassuring until you look at the table and the fixture list. Unbeaten can be useful. It can also be misleading. When home games against sides like Fulham end without three points, the gap opens quickly and the pressure follows.

Fulham came to Anfield, did their job, and left delighted. Liverpool had the ball, had the crowd, and still failed to impose themselves where it mattered. That is the issue. Clean sheets help, but sterile control does not win title races.

Reaction after full-time captured the frustration. Jermaine Pennant wrote, "I'm actually lost for words," before adding, "This is not acceptable, and if anyone says calm down we are unbeaten and it's only 4 games, then take your head for a wobble.

"Fulham are absolutely bang average, and leave Anfield on cloud 9. We have not won at Anfield in the prem yet."

It is blunt, but not hard to understand. Supporters can accept transition. What they do not accept easily is drift, especially at home.

There are positives. Liverpool have posted two straight clean sheets and have not lost in the league. Iraola is still bedding in his ideas and adapting to a bigger job, a different squad, and the added demands of European football in midweek.

Still, this is Liverpool. Patience exists, but only up to a point. The team may improve, and probably will improve, but early evidence says the rebuild is further from complete than many hoped. Right now, Liverpool are stable, organised, and unbeaten. They are also short of the level required to chase Arsenal properly.

title: CBF mourns death of former president Antônio Carlos Nunes
description: CBF vice president and the organization’s acting president on several occasions, Antônio Carlos Nunes, known as Colonel Nunes, has died at the age of 87Credits: CBFAntônio Carlos Nunes de Lima, be...
fullText:
CBF vice president and the organization's acting president on several occasions, Antônio Carlos Nunes, known as Colonel Nunes, has died at the age of 87Credits: CBF

Antônio Carlos Nunes de Lima, better known as Colonel Nunes, died in the early hours of this Sunday (13), at the age of 87, in Belém.

A reserve officer in the Military Police, he was born on November 21, 1938, in Monte Alegre, a city in the state of Pará where he also served as mayor.

A passionate Paysandu supporter, it was as a football executive that he made the greatest mark over the course of his career.

Nunes chaired the Pará Football Federation in different periods for nearly 20 years, was elected CBF vice president in December 2015, and served as acting president of Brazilian football's governing body for several months in 2016 and 2021, and between 2017 and 2019.

"CBF mourns the passing of Colonel Nunes, whose story was marked by strengthening football in his home state of Pará and in Brazil. At this moment of profound pain and sadness, we express our condolences to his family and friends," said CBF president Samir Xaud.

The wake will be held starting at 1 p.m. (Brasília time) this Sunday at the Max Domini memorial in Belém. He will be buried this Monday (14), in a ceremony at 11 a.m., at Recanto da Saudade cemetery, in the capital of Pará.

title: Team Europe beat United States to reclaim Solheim Cup
description: Team Europe produced a dominant display in Sunday's decisive singles to beat the United States and claim back the Solheim Cup after a dramatic three days of see-sawing fortunes.For only the seventh time, the teams came into Sunday's singles all-square at 8-8 after two nerve-jangling days at the Bernardus course.
fullText:
Team Europe produced a dominant display in Sunday's decisive singles to beat the United States and claim back the Solheim Cup after a dramatic three days of see-sawing fortunes.

Playing in her first Solheim Cup, Lottie Woad held her nerve to drain the putt on the 17th green to give Europe an unassailable lead over the Americans and snatch back the trophy.

The putt sparked wild scenes on the green as Woad was mobbed by her fellow players, cheered on by a raucous crowd at the first Solheim Cup hosted in the Netherlands.

For only the seventh time, the teams came into Sunday's singles all-square at 8-8 after two nerve-jangling days at the Bernardus course.

But Europe started strongly in the head-to-head battles, inspired by England star Charley Hull, who put a miserable weekend behind her to win her match and clinch the first European point.

World number one Nelly Korda showed her class to grab a point for the United States but it was not enough to stem the Europeans, who were too strong in the middle matches.

Woad had played with Hull in all four matches on Friday and Saturday and endured a torrid time, but she found redemption, rolling in the winning putt to beat Auston Kim in the battle of the rookies.

title: Medal rounds! ADCC 2026, Day 2 – live stream, BJJ results, video highlights
description: Join us for live results and highlights from the 2026 ADCC World Championships.

title: Andy Roddick Reveals Serena Williams’ ‘Really Cool’ Gesture To Frances Tiafoe In Locker Room After US Open Heartbreak
description: Andy Roddick has revealed Serena Williams’ “really cool” gesture toward Frances Tiafoe in the locker room following his heartbreaking U. S.
fullText:
Andy Roddick has revealed Serena Williams' "really cool" gesture toward Frances Tiafoe in the locker room following his heartbreaking U.S. Open semifinal loss.

Tiafoe enjoyed a strong run at the tournament, defeating Valentin Vacherot, Daniil Medvedev, and Alex Michelsen to reach the semifinals. However, his campaign ended on Friday when he lost to fellow American Ben Shelton at Arthur Ashe Stadium.

Shortly after the match, in the latest episode of 'Andy Roddick's Served' podcast, Roddick opened up about Williams' supportive gesture toward Tiafoe. Revealing that she went to the men's locker room to console him, the former tennis player said:

"The reason she was in there was to console Frances. That's the reason she was in the locker room. It wasn't just all fun good times and to crush me. She was in there to talk to Frances, which I thought was really cool of her," said Roddick.

Williams also competed in the women's and mixed doubles events at the U.S. Open. She partnered with her sister, Venus Williams, in women's doubles, where they suffered a first-round exit. She then teamed up with Carlos Alcaraz in mixed doubles, with the pair reaching the quarterfinals before losing to Belinda Bencic and Flavio Cobolli.

The semifinal between Tiafoe and Shelton also marked a historic moment for Black tennis. The two Americans became the first Black American men to meet in a Grand Slam semifinal in the Open Era. By defeating Tiafoe, Shelton became the first Black American man to reach the U.S. Open final since Arthur Ashe in 1972.

After losing to Shelton in the U.S. Open semifinals, Frances Tiafoe spoke about the defeat during his post-match press conference. Praising his fellow American's performance, he explained how difficult the match was.

"It's hard. Obviously I have been in this position a lot now, thankfully, but also it's tough. I wanted to be in a Grand Slam final, obviously, it is a big match. But I got to give it to Ben. Played well. He served really well tonight, which made it really tough for me and I did not serve great. So I was just trying to hang in there on my service games, but ultimately we didn't say much," said Frances Tiafoe.

Reflecting on his season, he added:

"At the same time it's been a great season for me, but also this one is tough. I wanted to win this one. These last couple of weeks have been great weeks but I have not been able to finish and that is probably going to be the next thing for me."

Ahead of his U.S. Open run, Frances Tiafoe competed at the Cincinnati Open, where he lost to Arthur Fils in the final on Aug. 24.

title: World championship leader Antonelli wins Spanish GP
description: Kimi Antonelli extended his lead in the world championship with his eighth victory of the season at the Spanish Formula One Grand Prix at the Madring on Sunday.Seven-time world champion Lewis Hamilton, who had scored points in every race this season, missed out completely, retiring his Ferrari on lap seven because of brake failure.
fullText:
Kimi Antonelli extended his lead in the world championship with his eighth victory of the season at the Spanish Formula One Grand Prix at the Madring on Sunday.

The 20-year-old Mercedes driver finished clear of Max Verstappen (Red Bull) and Lando Norris (McLaren) and is now 81 points ahead of nearest rival, his Mercedes teammate George Russell, in the title race.

Ferrari's Charles Leclerc (Ferrari) finished fourth ahead of fellow Briton Russell and Liam Lawson in the second Red Bull.

Franco Colapinto (Alpine), Oscar Piastri (McLaren), Arvid Lindblad (Racing Bulls) and Niko Hulkenberg (Audi) rounded out the top 10.

Seven-time world champion Lewis Hamilton, who had scored points in every race this season, missed out completely, retiring his Ferrari on lap seven because of brake failure.

George Russell was another big loser, with the Mercedes driver suffering badly from his team's decision to put him on two-stop strategy - the only one of the main runners to have this - which blew his chances of podium and left him even further behind his teammate in the title race.

Norris will also rue his team's poor strategy.

The reigning world champion drove a blistering lap on Saturday to claim pole position and was leading comfortably until the intervention of the virtual safety car (VSC) on lap 15.

While Antonelli and Verstappen immediately dived into the pits to change their tyres McLaren kept Norris out for an extra lap.

As he prepared to come in, the VSC finished meaning he lost time against his rivals, and the Briton wasn't helped by a slow pitstop of seven seconds.

He clawed his way past Russell and moved into third when Leclerc finally boxed on lap 48 of the 57, at which point the lead was handed to Antonelli who cruised home to take the chequered flag.

title: Officers will enforce parking rules and no-fly zones on Jags game day, JSO says
description: Jacksonville police remind Jaguars fans to park legally and avoid flying drones near the stadium on game day.
fullText:
The Jacksonville Sheriff's Office is reminding fans heading to the Jaguars game today to plan ahead for parking and to leave their drones at home.

JSO said officers will be stationed throughout the area on game day to enforce parking rules, saying, "we don't want to write you a ticket or tow your car, but we will."

Fans are encouraged to decide on a parking plan before leaving home.

Approved parking is available in lots around the stadium for those with pre-purchased passes, as well as in private lots around the Downtown Sports Complex.

Parking is prohibited in medians, shoulders, right-of-ways, and on bridges. Alternatives to game-day parking include the Gameday Xpress, water taxi service and ride-share options.

Drones will not be permitted in or around the stadium on game day.

The Federal Aviation Administration has established a no-fly zone extending three nautical miles from the stadium, in effect from 12 p.m. Sunday until one hour after the game concludes.

Fans who notice drones in the air near the stadium during the game should not be alarmed — the Sheriff's Office said those aircraft belong to authorities working to ensure the safety of fans, players and officials.

Anyone who sees suspicious activity Sunday is asked to notify a nearby officer.
