title: Kahleah Copper wants to play with joy
description: LOS ANGELES -- The Phoenix Mercury visited the Los Angeles Sparks last month at the Galen Center in the University of Southern California.
fullText:
LOS ANGELES -- The Phoenix Mercury visited the Los Angeles Sparks last month at the Galen Center in the University of Southern California. A lot changed from their visit before that a couple of weeks before to their game at USC.

For Kahleah Copper, a lot changed for her as well. Hours after their game against the Sparks on July 22nd, Copper was named to the All-Star team as she replaced her friend, then-Sparks guard Kelsey Plum.

About a week after All-Star weekend, Plum was traded to the Mercury and the friends were suddenly teammates.

"(Plum brought) her energy, her vibes, her leadership, her championship experience (to the team)," Copper said before their game against the Sparks at USC. "She knows what it takes to win. I'm glad to play alongside with her."

As for All-Star Weekend after expecting to get some rest?

"It was cool. It was a good experience," Copper said about that weekend. "There were a lot of good people."

The Mercury are out of the playoff chase but Copper still wants to build momentum towards the end of their season.

"I think we've got to play with some joy," Copper said about the rest of the campaign. "We've got to compete harder and play with joy. Just have that toughness, play with that energy."

While this W season won't end with a title for Copper, she's part of Team USA, who is playing in the gold medal round on Sunday. She scored nine of her 13 points in that all-important second half against Spain in the semifinal round. At the very least, Copper is making winning plays in the international stage. She's averaging 7.8 points and 4.4 rebounds in five games of the World Cup.

Not only does she get joy in playing but there's joy on the men's stage, too. LeBron James signed with the Sixers in free agency and Copper, a Philly girl, was very happy about that result.

"I'm excited that he's in the city," Copper beamed. "I'm excited to see the Sixers win and try to compete in the championship. Let's not forget about Jaylen Brown. I'm super excited to see that team come together. I'm planning on being courtside."

And America is planning on being courtside for Copper and a possible gold medal from the FIBA World Cup on Sunday as they try to defeat France for all the marbles.

title: Noche UFC bonuses: Slick Silva sub snags six figures
description: After months of events with tons of finishes, Noche UFC hit a slowdown with just four stoppages in Arizona.
fullText:
Noche UFC bonuses: Slick Silva sub snags six figures

The UFC handed out four bonuses after Saturday's card in Arizona, including one to the main event winner.

After UFC Fight Night 288, the promotion's annual Noche UFC event, four fighters picked up an extra $100,000 for their performances at Desert Diamond Arena in Glendale, Ariz. Additionally, two fighters got $25,000 extra checks for finishes that weren't bonus-winners.

Check out the list of winners below.

Tommy McMillen (12-0 MMA, 3-0 UFC) got a stiff test from Marwan Rahiki (9-1 MMA, 2-1 UFC), but survived a back-and-forth bloody scrap for a unanimous decision – and his third $100,000 bonus in three UFC fights. Quick reaction from the MMA community had the bout ticketed for a Fight of the Year candidate.

Jean Silva (18-3 MMA, 7-1 UFC) took a long time to get started against Jose Delgado (12-3 MMA, 4-2 UFC), who dropped him in the first round. But Silva slowly started to take over in the third, and after he stunned Delgado with a punch, he sank in a one-armed rear-naked choke.

Sean King III (7-0 MMA, 1-0 UFC) was supposed to fight on DWCS. Instead, he took a short-notice UFC fight against Jessie Rosas (8-2-1 MMA, 0-1 UFC) and delivered one of the most vicious finishes of the year in just 36 seconds. King

Tommy Gantt (13-0 MMA, 2-0 UFC) expertly took Drakkar Klose (16-4-1 MMA, 10-4 UFC) down in the third round, then choked him out with an inverted triangle.

Yousri Belgaroui (11-3 MMA, 3-0 UFC) was a massive 9-1 favorite over Djorden Santos (11-4 MMA, 1-3 UFC) in their middleweight fight on the prelims and showed why when he pummeled him on the feet for a TKO late in the first round.

title: Ohio State vs. Texas three and out halftime review | Buckeyes Wire
description: It's halftime in Austin, Texas, and here's three things that we took from Ohio State vs. Texas through the first 30 minutes of play.
fullText:
It's halftime in Austin with Ohio State and Texas engaging in one of the most anticipated nonconference games of the college football season. The Buckeyes used some Longhorn mistakes and some excellent play on both sides of the ball to take a 20-3 lead into the locker room, which is banking the national narrative in this one.

We like to look back on the first half and take three observations and takeaways from what we saw through the first 30 minutes of action, and in this case, there's plenty to talk about. Here are three observations from what we saw from the Buckeyes and Longhorns in the first half of what should be one whale of a second half to finish this thing out.

Ohio State forces a fumble against Texas on the first play of the game😤

(via ESPN) pic.twitter.com/kxvE7F9D0B

The defense hasn't been very stingy in stopping the run through the middle, but it has been very opportunistic in forcing two turnovers. Both of them led to two scores and have really been the difference in the game so far. You have to think that the turnovers aren't going to continue, so Ohio State will have to continue to make plays while getting equal possessions.

Jeremiah Smith: Freakshow

(Via: ABC)pic.twitter.com/jQuJSiQ1A4

A lot of the talk coming into this game was the ability of Texas to limit Smith the last two times these teams matched up. So far, that hasn't been the case in this one. Jeremiah Smith had six catches for 110 yards and a touchdown in the first half and is a big part of the game plan.

Offensive coordinator Arthur Smith is doing a great job of moving him around and creating mismatches, and the Texas defense has really had no answer for it. We'll see if there are halftime adjustments made because if Julian Sayin continues to find Smith, it's hard to think the Longhorns can pull this one out.

ARCH MANNING WITH A BULLET BUT RYAN WINGO DROPS IT.....pic.twitter.com/JvDidKva62

Texas has not played good football, and that's the reason this game is in Ohio State's favor. We already talked about the two turnovers, but there have been a couple of dropped passes, missed assignments on defense, and Arch Manning has misfired on some key throws.

Don't expect that to continue, and it feels like the Buckeyes should be up by more. Let's hope the defense continues to play well and that the offense can finish off drives because this one feels like it's going to tighten up.

title: Braylan Lovelace, defense prop up Pitt in 12-7 win over UCF
description: A week after Pitt’s offense starred, the Panthers’ defense wanted its shine, too.
fullText:
This article originally appeared on PittsburghSportsNOW.com.

A week after Pitt's offense starred, the Panthers' defense wanted its shine, too.

During a 12-7, rain-soaked win over UCF at home on Saturday night, Pat Narduzzi's resistance held the Knights to 20 rushing yards on 22 attempts, 4-for-13 on third down and 0-3 on fourth.

The Knights, who scored 73 points in their season-opening win over Bethune-Cookman, couldn't dent the scoreboard until under three minutes remained in the contest and managed just 206 total yards.

"We've gotta get better," Knights coach Scott Frost told ESPN2 of his side's ground game at the beginning of the fourth quarter. "It's kinda too late for that now. We've just gotta call the best stuff we've got, and try to make some plays. We've had some things there and haven't hit them. … Their blitzes have worked, and we haven't run the ball."

On the offensive side of the ball for Pitt, Damon Ferguson Jr., a true freshman and On3's No. 14 running back in the 2026 class, surprisingly started at running back, as sophomore Ja'Kyrian "Boosie" Turner. Narduzzi told ESPN2 that holding Turner out was "kind of a game-time decision."

With the help of his blockers — who helped shove him in — Ferguson scored his first collegiate rushing touchdown, from 13 yards out, with 28 seconds remaining in the first half.

title: Player Ratings: Real Madrid 4–1 Rayo Vallecano
description: Real Madrid beat Rayo Vallecano 4–1 at the Bernabéu, with Kylian Mbappé delivering two goals and an assist, Álvaro Carreras making an electric start, and Arda Güler producing a spectacular cameo off the bench. The scoreline was convincing, though Rayo’s second-half improvement ensured Thibaut Courtois still had plenty of work to do. Thibaut Courtois — […]
fullText:
Real Madrid beat Rayo Vallecano 4–1 at the Bernabéu, with Kylian Mbappé delivering two goals and an assist, Álvaro Carreras making an electric start, and Arda Güler producing a spectacular cameo off the bench. The scoreline was convincing, though Rayo's second-half improvement ensured Thibaut Courtois still had plenty of work to do.

Made six important saves as Rayo grew into the game in the second half. Madrid's attacking output will get most of the attention, but Courtois was still required to intervene regularly and delivered when called upon.

Defended well on the wing and finished with three tackles. Nearly added a goal with a towering header from an Arda Güler set piece. A solid contribution at both ends.

Strong in his duels and handled his defensive responsibilities well, though he did not have a particularly heavy workload, especially in the first half.

A monster in the air. Finished with a whopping 12 clearances and was consistently on hand to deal with deliveries into the box.

An electric start: won the penalty for Madrid's opener, then combined with Kylian Mbappé to score the team's second goal. His attacking contributions were the headline, but he also won five of his seven ground duels. An excellent performance.

Stepped up to press effectively and got himself into good attacking positions. Mourinho withdrew him at half-time as an injury precaution rather than for anything related to his performance. His absence was felt after the break.

Very tidy with his progression and distribution. Helped Madrid move the ball forward cleanly and initiated the move for the third goal from deep. Not the flashiest contribution of the evening, but an important one.

Dazzled the Bernabéu with his dribbling on his first start and won the crowd over with his defensive work rate. Finished with two key passes and one wayward shot. Plenty of encouragement, even with room to sharpen the end product. Baby steps.

Unstoppable ball-carrying, a brilliant goal, and the usual relentless defensive hustle. Bellingham brought both attacking quality and a willingness to do the less glamorous work.

Docked half a point for the mistake that led to Rayo's goal, but his first-half performance was excellent. Pressed aggressively in the build-up to Madrid's opener and provided the assist for the third goal. A major attacking influence, despite the costly error.

Two goals, an assist, and only the crossbar standing between him and a hat-trick. Clinical in front of goal, while also turning provider for Carreras on Madrid's second. An outstanding attacking performance.

Madrid suffered after he replaced Valverde in midfield, though that was not solely his responsibility. Distributed the ball well and won a couple of important ground duels, but the team did not maintain the same control after the change.

Helped close out the game with his defensive presence and distribution. A useful contribution to settle things down.

An absolute fireball off the bench. Completely changed the game and produced five key passes—the most of anyone on the pitch—in just 18 minutes. Also finished with an assist. An extraordinary amount of creativity packed into a brief appearance.

title: Georgia Tech's Jaylen Mbakwe leaves game on stretcher vs Tennessee football
description: Georgia Tech cornerback Jaylen Mbakwe exited the game vs. Tennessee football on a stretcher after suffering an apparent head injury.
fullText:
ATLANTA − Georgia Tech cornerback Jaylen Mbakwe was taken off the field on a stretcher in the third quarter of game against Tennessee football at Bobby Dodd Stadium on Sept. 12.

Play stopped at the 14:17 mark of the third quarter and UT driving with a 24-10 lead. Mbakwe hit his head on the knee of Georgia Tech defensive end Jordan Walker, who also exited with a lower body injury, during a play.

Trainers tended to Mbakwe on the field for a few minutes before calling for a stretcher to take him off the field. Mbakwe was able to move both his hands as he left the field. He signaled to the crowd and gripped a trainer's hand .

Mbakwe was taken to Grady Memorial Hospital, two miles away from Bobby Dodd Stadium, according to the ESPN broadcast.

title: Rams Defensive Coordinator Under Fire After Disappointing Start
description: The Los Angeles Rams were massively disappointing on both ends of the field, culminating in a 27-7 loss to the San Fransico 49ers. The post Rams Defensive Coordinator Under Fire After Disappointing Start appeared first on LA Sports Report.
fullText:
The Los Angeles Rams were massively disappointing on both ends of the field, culminating in a 27-7 loss to the San Fransico 49ers.

However, given all of the additions to the defense, that was the side with the higher expectations.

Aaron Donald returned, albeit not for Week 1, while the best defensive player in the sport, Myles Garrett, was added via trade, along with two good cornerbacks in Jaylen Watson and Trent McDuffie.

In 2025, this unit was already one of the better groups in the league, and with so many upgrades, it was expected to be a super unit.

The Rams allowed 27 points and had only a 5.6% pressure rate, dwarfed by the 49ers' 27.6% rate. The Niners totaled 379 yards and 5.9 yards per play as well.

On third down, SF converted seven of 12 scenarios. The Rams allowed more explosive plays, and they had no answers in the run game.

After the Rams' loss, ESPN analyst Dan Orlovsky said the defense was a bigger concern than the offense, specifically calling out Los Angeles defensive coordinator Chris Shula.

"I am very concerned about that defense, and I'm very concerned about their defensive coordinator," Orlovsky said on ESPN's "Get Up!" 

"The last four games that we have watched this defense on the field with all kinds of talent, they have stunk. Bryce Young lit them up. Caleb Williams lit them up. Sam Darnold lit them up. Brock Purdy lit them up."

While Orlovsky is right that the Rams have disappointed in some marquee games defensively, this season is only one game old, and much more is to come from Shula.

The team stayed in heavy zone coverage rather than mixing in much man, which let the 49ers gash them.

The defensive scheme looked quite vanilla for the Rams overall, and they are known for hiding things they'll do throughout the season early on.

All eyes will be on what adjustments they make once Donald enters the mix and Donald gets healthy.

fullText:
Tricolor clash: Bahia and Fortaleza face off in the 2026 Copa do Nordeste U-20 final Credits: @jhonypinhofotografo/Disclosure/Instagram/@ecbahia and Baggio Rodrigues / Fortaleza EC

Bahia and Fortaleza will play in the final of the 14th edition of the Copa do Nordeste U-20. The two tricolor sides qualified on Saturday afternoon (12), in matches played in the city of Feira de Santana.

At Jóia da Princesa, Esquadrão de Aço beat Náutico 4-3 on penalties, while Leão do Pici defeated Estrela de Março-BA 3-1 at Arena Cajueiro, with goals from Luis Filipe, Filipi and Juan. Rikelme scored for the team from Bahia.

This will be the second tournament final between Bahia and Fortaleza. In 2018, the Ceará side won the title: they prevailed 4-2 on penalties after a 2-2 draw in regular time. In addition to that triumph, they also lifted the trophy in 2005. Bahia, meanwhile, were champions of the inaugural edition in 2001.

The final will be played over two legs, with the tentative dates set for September 19 and 26, respectively. Bahia will host the second match because they had a better campaign than Fortaleza.

title: US Open champ Rybakina on top of world after injury scare
description: Elena Rybakina is on top of the tennis world, celebrating her first US Open title and her rise to number one barely more than three weeks after she feared injury would force her out of the final Grand Slam of the year.Kazakhstan's Rybakina beat two-time defending champion Aryna Sabalenka 6-4, 5-7, 6-2 on Saturday to claim her third Grand Slam title.
fullText:
Elena Rybakina is on top of the tennis world, celebrating her first US Open title and her rise to number one barely more than three weeks after she feared injury would force her out of the final Grand Slam of the year.

Kazakhstan's Rybakina beat two-time defending champion Aryna Sabalenka 6-4, 5-7, 6-2 on Saturday to claim her third Grand Slam title.

She'd already assured herself of toppling Sabalenka from the number one spot just by reaching the semi-finals.

"I can't find words right now, honestly," Rybakina said. "I don't expect nothing like this coming to this tournament. I've been dealing with a little bit with an injury, but somehow everything aligned together on my side."

The "little bit of an injury" saw Rybakina hobble out of her Cincinnati quarter-final on August 20 -- 10 days before the start of the US Open -- unable to put weight on her left heel.

"It wasn't the best time, for sure, because I was so upset," Rybakina said. "I didn't know actually how it's going to be day by day.

"We arrive to New York. We did MRI. It didn't look that great. We had to talk with a lot of doctors to get opinion what we should do."

With a doctor in Australia providing valuable long-distance advice, Rybakina and her team came up with a plan to manage her training, rest and treatment and give her a chance at her second major title of the year, after her victory over Sabalenka at the Australian Open.

Her run to the final included an impressive fourth-round victory over two-time champion Naomi Osaka before come-from-behind wins over resurgent Olympic gold medallist Zheng Qinwen and former champion Coco Gauff.

It all led to her 18th showdown with Sabalenka in a rivalry that has emerged as the most dynamic on the WTA tour.

Having narrowed Sabalenka's lead in their head to 10-8, Rybakina is looking forward to more chances to take on her fiery rival, whose on-court personality is the perfect foil to her own cool approach.

"I don't know what the future will bring, but it's always very difficult matches against Aryna," she said. "I feel like we push each other to be better after such tough battles."

The two seem destined to tussle for the top spot for some time. But other players -- Gauff and Jessica Pegula -- also had a chance to seize the number one ranking in New York, so Rybakina knows that Sabalenka is not the only rival she must be wary of.

"I feel like not only with her, with also other players, top players, you always want to try something new, to change in your game, to be better," she said.

"I don't know what future is going to bring, but I hope success and some more wins."

title: MSU ground game wakes up, runs over Eastern Michigan after halftime
description: Cam Edwards rushed for 152 yards and two touchdowns in a 35-7 win over Eastern Michigan.
fullText:
EAST LANSING — Ten yards from the end zone, Michigan State running back Cam Edwards strained as three defenders tried to wrangle him to the ground in the backfield. He dove forward toward the line of scrimmage with seemingly all his might. It wound up costing him. For the first time in Edwards' five-year college career, he fumbled.

If that fumble pierced Edwards' perfection protecting the football, then he made up for it the next play: a 40-yard gain that set up the final touchdown of Michigan State's 35-7 win over Eastern Michigan at Spartan Stadium on Saturday, Sept. 12. He finished the game with 21 carries for 152 yards and two scores. Both are season highs, two games into his Spartan career.

"It's not acceptable," Edwards said of the fumble. "I was beating myself up about it, but I think I did a really good way of responding for the team and just putting that play aside."

In a game MSU only led 14-7 at halftime, both outgained and out-possessed by a Mid-American Conference team it entered a 17½-point favorite against, Michigan State turned to its run game to lead it forward. It ran for 198 yards in the second half, and 258 of its 472 total yards in the entire game.

All those rushing yards offered redemption for an offense that prides itself on running the football. And for Edwards, who prides himself on protecting it.

"We didn't want his last touch to be what happened there," MSU coach Pat Fitzgerald said.

Three of Michigan State's five touchdowns came on the ground, two of those direct snaps to Edwards. He rushed in a 1-yard touchdown to take a 14-0 lead midway through the second quarter and added a 2-yard gain in the third.

"When I was in high school, I used to play a little bit of quarterback, and we used to do a little bit of wildcat," Edwards said of the genesis of those looks. "So you know, I kind of just stretched it over to Coach (Nick) Sheridan, and was just making a joke out of it. And then he actually took it really serious."

So did Eastern Michigan. Michigan State called 45 runs to 26 passing plays. However, the Spartans had only mustered 60 yards rushing by halftime compared to 107 by the Eagles. In the second half, Eastern Michigan saw more of the team it expected to see: one that feeds itself through its gifted tailback Edwards.

"I think what they want to be is downhill running, tough, physical — you know what I mean?" Eastern Michigan coach Chris Creighton said. "Big Ten, Michigan State football, right? And I think that you can see that just in the first two games."

"We took their best punch in the second quarter," Fitzgerald said. "And again, credit to Coach Creighton and the staff."

Already, Michigan State is up to 408 rushing yards through two games, with 250 of those and three touchdowns belonging to Edwards on 48 carries. Twenty-one of those carries came Saturday, and the Spartans plan on many more for the bell cow. Two of those — the aforementioned 40-yarder and a 33-yard gain in the third quarter — accounted for nearly half his yards Saturday and both led to touchdown drives.

"It makes it a lot easier on me to go out there and win a game when you got a guy like this guy running for I don't know how many it was, but I know it's a lot," quarterback Alessio Milivojevic said of Edwards. "You got Marv (Parrish), Jazz (Patterson), and the guys in front that played their butt off. So I think it just makes it easier on me, and I think together, mixing the run and pass, it makes it a tough offense to stop."

More: Cam Edwards aims to be 'best running back in the country' for Spartans

All three of those touchdowns, surprisingly, have come on direct snaps. If Michigan State is skipping the middle man on some looks, Milivojevic hopes his running back doesn't get too carried away.

"This guy thinks he's a quarterback, but I think he's a pretty good running back," Milivojevic joked. "So hopefully he can stay in that position."

title: Maryland volleyball takes down Princeton, 3-0, for 6th win of 2026
description: The victory marked the Terps’ fourth succesive straight set victory for the first time since 2023.
fullText:
Sydney Bryant was the spark behind Maryland volleyball's offensive momentum, leading an attack that overwhelmed Princeton throughout Saturday night's match.

The Terps came out on top in straight sets and are now 6-1 to begin the season, their best start since 2021. Head coach Adam Hughes had high praise for Maryland's confidence in the locker room and on the court this year.

"I'll give a lot of the shoutout to the seniors. In the beginning of the year, we talked about how freshmen were going to be a big factor and how the seniors are going to have to be big leaders and be composed, and they've done that. It's been at practice, it's been at meetings, it's been across the board — not just how we perform in matches," Hughes said.

Maryland shot out to an early lead, kicked off by a kill from Melby that was followed by a service ace from Brooklynne Brass. Two service errors later placed Princeton in a 5-1 deficit to begin the match.

Duru Gökçen and Eva Rohrbach posed a threatening blocking duo at the net in the first set and anchored an effective defensive unit that halted multiple attacks from the Tigers. Their blocking led to a kill from Sara Toth that forced Princeton to call a timeout as the Terps took a 9-3 lead.

Rohrbach came out of the timeout with a kill, giving the Terps more energy to ride off of. Veteran outside hitter Bryant led by example with three crucial kills. They, along with a kill and service ace from Melby and a kill from Rohrbach, allowed Maryland to take an 11-point lead, their largest of the set.

Princeton attempted to make a late surge and steal the set, cutting the lead to as little as six with a kill from Erin McNair. However, a late push from Princeton was not enough to stifle the Terps' momentum. Errors by the Tigers and Maryland's aggressive defense allowed the Terps to close out the first set, 25-17.

The second set had a more balanced start in comparison to the opening set. Gameplay was back-and-forth for the first few points. Toth assisted on three kills – two from Melby, and one from Rohrbach – to spark a 3-0 run that allowed the Terps to briefly pull away from the stalemate that characterized the start of the set.

Maryland couldn't yet fully break away as it did in the first set, though. Tigers outside hitter Sarah Hom cutMaryland's lead to two points. Unfortunately for Princeton, the pause in the Terps' momentum wouldn't last for long. With a kill from Gökçen and Raina Chwialkowski recording a series of points through service and errors by the Tigers, the Terps went on an 8-2 run.

Princeton wouldn't recover from the deficit the run caused. Bryant added three kills to her impressive total late in the set that allowed Maryland to pull away. Ashtyn Syms attempted to spark some momentum for Princeton with a kill to fend off a set point by Maryland. However, Melby secured her eighth kill of the game as Maryland secured its second-set win, 25-15.

The Tigers took their first lead of the match with two kills from Clark Taylor. This would be the first and only advantage for Princeton, as Maryland was able to pull away and capitalize on the Tigers' errors. Those errors sparked a 7-1 run for the Terps, as Bryant and Gökçen added kills to increase the lead.

Action was balanced for the middle portion of the third set. Attack errors from both sides kept the Maryland lead around five points until two errors from Princeton's Ashtyn Sims landed the Terps a 20-13 lead late in the set. The Tigers fought back, with crucial kills from Taylor and McNair that brought Maryland's lead to three as Princeton attempted to steal the set from the Terps. Instead, the Tigers' hopes would fall short as two errors gave Maryland the deciding points to rise to victory in a 25-20 third set.

1. Team chemistry. Communication between Toth and Maryland's veteran outside hitters Melby and Bryant allowed the two to combine for 23 kills in an aggressive attack that was almost unstoppable. When asked about what went well offensively today, Bryant praised Toth.

"There was a lot of communication between us and our setter. She's not afraid to go back to us, and that clear line of communication really helped," Bryant said.

2. Big-time blocking. Maryland's blocking core in Gökçen and Rohrbach fended off fierce attacks from Princeton and earned crucial points for the Terps that sparked runs.

3. Attacking versatility. Hughes was able to rely on Bryant and Melby for individual point production at different moments throughout the match, allowing the veterans to rest and balance the offensive load.

title: From struggling to walk to lifting trophy - how Rybakina triumphed
description: Elena Rybakina arrived in New York unable to walk without pain after injuring her foot. She leaves the city as the US Open champion and new world number one.
fullText:
Elena Rybakina arrived in New York unable to walk without pain after injuring her foot. She leaves the city as the US Open champion and new world number one.

Kazakhstan's Rybakina produced a brilliant performance to beat two-time defending champion Aryna Sabalenka 6-4 5-7 6-2 in Saturday's final and repeat her Australian Open success against the same player in January.

Clutching the trophy on Saturday night, Rybakina reflected that "some magic is happening" for her after her difficult lead-in to the tournament.

The 27-year-old aggravated a foot injury during her quarter-final in Cincinnati against Iga Swiatek last month, a little over a week before the final major of the year began.

Playing on through injury could have disastrous consequences for the rest of the season - but Rybakina, knowing the top ranking was in her grasp, wanted to try and play in the final Grand Slam of the year.

"I was so upset. I didn't know actually how it was going to be day by day," she said.

"We arrived in New York and did an MRI. It didn't look that great.

"I couldn't even walk for the next few days without pain.

"I was lucky enough to have a very good doctor in Australia. She was on the phone with us all the time and somehow, with the team, we made a plan."

Rybakina did not do any on-court training for a week but daily recovery sessions in the gym - plus trips for dinner and to the cinema to "switch the mind" - helped get her ready for another major triumph.

She won her first four matches at Flushing Meadows without dropping a set, including seeing off four-time major winner Naomi Osaka.

Her run from then on - which included beating Olympic champion Zheng Qinwen in the quarter-finals, outlasting third seed Coco Gauff in the semis and outplaying top seed Sabalenka in the final - was nothing short of outstanding.

"I was so unlucky with the injury, but I'm very proud," Rybakina said.

Listen: US Open podcast - Rybakina crowned champion

American Shelton to face Zverev in US Open final

Rybakina had already been confirmed as world number one by reaching the semi-finals in New York. The fact that her final opponent was Sabalenka, the player she will replace at the top of the rankings, added an extra dimension to Saturday's championship match.

Rybakina won the first set despite her serve, one of her biggest weapons, misfiring.

She landed only 27% of her first serves during the opener, but still won 22 of 30 points behind her serve and did not face a break point as she took the lead.

Sabalenka eventually broke in the 12th game of the second set to send their match the distance, but Rybakina who dominated the decider.

While the Belarusian grew visibly more frustrated as the final slipped away, Rybakina remained remarkably composed.

"The way she [Rybakina] quietly walks around, she doesn't really lift her head up and she gives no emotion away whatsoever," former British number one Annabel Croft said on BBC Radio 5 Live.

"Rybakina is like a machine out there. You never know what's going on in her head."

However, nerves did show when Rybakina threw in two double faults as she served for the title.

At 40-30, the trophy in her sights, Rybakina could have blinked. Instead, she cooly sent down her 12th ace of the match to secure her third Grand Slam title.

The second seed produced her biggest celebration of her three major wins - a smile and both arms raised in celebration as she took in the applause.

Rybakina has now won two of her three Grand Slam finals against Sabalenka, all of which have come on their favoured hard courts.

On Monday, Rybakina will become the 30th different women to top the world rankings.

She is a different personality to Sabalenka, who held the position for the past 99 weeks, but Croft believes she will "take it in her stride".

"I actually think she has the right personality to deal with it," Croft said.

"There are going to be a lot of players around her nipping at her heels. She can fluctuate with her levels, but when it really matters, we've seen her be able to bring it to the table.

"It's not going to be easy to hang onto it. I think women's tennis is really exciting right now."

Rybakina has completed three parts of the career Grand Slam, with just a French Open victory missing from her collection.

After winning Wimbledon in 2022, she did not claim her second major until January's Australian Open, and has now added a third in New York.

She has never previously been further than the quarter-finals at Roland Garros, although she did win a WTA 1000 event on clay in Rome in 2023.

Former British number one Laura Robson said on Sky Sports: "She is an all-surface player - clay is the worst one, but when you get her on something that's quite lively or quick, she's unplayable at times.

"I genuinely think she will win many more Slams. I just don't see, when her serve and return are on, how pretty much anyone can beat her on a hard court."

GB's Hewett beats Oda to win fifth US Open title

title: NYPD identifies Palestinian flag-waving man who charged Yankee Stadium field on 9/11 anniversary
description: Police identify Palestinian flag-waving man who charged Yankee Stadium field on 9/11 anniversary
fullText:
New York City Police have identified the Palestinian flag-waving man who charged the Yankee Stadium field on the 25th anniversary of 9/11 Friday night, according to reports.

Kelly Marcucci, 38, of Long Island ran onto the left field grass precisely at 9:11 p.m. during the 7th inning of the Mets-Yankees game. He was wearing a "No Kings" shirt and waving a Palestinian flag and was promptly tackled by security before the crowd broke into chants of "USA, USA."

He is facing misdemeanor charges for interference with a professional sporting event and trespassing, the Post reported.

Fans seated above the Mets bullpen threw beer on him after security moved him off the field and beyond the outfield fence.

Marcucci's Facebook page on Friday included a rant referencing "late-stage capitalism," "Trump," "Joe Rogan," and "Saudi Arabia," among other things.

The Yankees won the game 6-4 in the first game of the Subway Series.

Prior to the game, Joe Torre, Tino Martinez, Scott Brosius, Mariano Rivera and Derek Jeter were announced to the Yankee Stadium crowd.

U.S. Open finalist Ben Shelton says it's 'not easy' playing in front of Jalen BrunsonSep. 12, 2026, 7:29 a.m.

Derek Jeter reflects on 9/11 emotions: 'We took that responsibility seriously'Sep. 11, 2026, 10:05 a.m.

Aaron Judge Gerrit Cole, and Aaron Boone also laid a wreath at the 9/11 Monument in Monument Park honor of the 2,977 who lost their lives that day.

"Certainly understand the weight of today and certainly being the 25th anniversary," Boone told reporters pre-game, "but having the two New York teams here playing, having lived through being a baseball player at the time, knowing the role that baseball played at the time, it feels like an honor to go out there tonight.

"I understand there will be a lot of different emotions in the building tonight with a lot of people with a lot of different contexts in and around that day, so we don't take lightly walking out on that field."

title: Rybakina wins US Open to inflict further pain on Sabalenka
description: Elena Rybakina demonstrates why she is the best women's player in the world by beating Aryna Sabalenka to win her first US Open title.
fullText:
Elena Rybakina demonstrated why she is the best women's player in the world by beating two-time defending champion Aryna Sabalenka to win her first US Open title.

Kazakhstan's Rybakina already knew she would be the new world number one after Saturday's final regardless of the result, and she celebrated with a 6-4 5-7 6-2 victory over the player she will replace.

Rybakina was the more composed of the two throughout as she claimed the third Grand Slam title of her career, having triumphed at Wimbledon in 2022 and the Australian Open earlier this year.

Sabalenka hoped to soften the blow of losing the top ranking by winning a third consecutive US Open title - but looked fraught in a tense performance.

Rybakina and Sabalenka have developed a strong rivalry built not only on their outstanding talent but their contrasting personalities.

And Rybakina's ice-cool composure - the direct opposite of the Belarusian's combustible nature - was a key difference as she took control at Flushing Meadows.

Rybakina stayed calm in an opening set where her first serve let her down and, despite her biggest weapon not firing on all cylinders, was able to execute a devastating returning game which left Sabalenka frustrated.

Sabalenka's groundstrokes improved as Rybakina's level dropped slightly in a tighter second set, taking her third opportunity to force a decider when she swarmed over Rybakina's second serve in the 12th game.

But the loose shots from Sabalenka reappeared in the third set - as did the negativity.

Rybakina's deep returning pinned Sabalenka to the baseline as she broke for a 2-1 lead, which allowed the incoming world number one to grow in stature.

There was a sign of nerves when Rybakina produced a double fault on her first championship point, but she reset admirably to hammer down an ace and underline her status as the best player in the world.

From struggling to walk to lifting trophy - how Rybakina triumphed

Listen to All About US Open: Rybakina crowned champion as Sabalenka melts down

Rybakina rarely shows emotion on the court but there was a brief flash of a smile as she clinched her second major victory of an outstanding 2026 season.

That illustrated the sense of satisfaction she felt after winning a title few had predicted - not only because she had never previously gone beyond the last 16 in New York but the circumstances coming into the final major of the season.

With her penetrating serve and thunderous groundstrokes, Rybakina has a brand of first-strike tennis that can take the racquet out of anyone's hands.

Therefore it has been a surprise she has not enjoyed greater success on the Flushing Meadows hard courts, perhaps a result of her personality not being particularly suited to the brash nature of New York.

"I was coming here for the last 10 years and it was never successful. I'm falling in love with New York more and more," Rybakina, 27, said.

What makes the second seed's victory even more remarkable is that she was unsure if she would be fit enough to even play.

Rybakina was unable to walk for several days after injuring her ankle in the Cincinnati Open quarter-finals, putting her chances of competing here in serious jeopardy.

Not only was Rybakina able to play, but she cruised through her opening four matches thanks to a huge service game that rarely allowed opponents to get into points.

Rybakina's next two wins over China's Zheng Qinwen and home favourite Coco Gauff required more work after losing the first sets, proving she had the durability to come through tough battles.

Against Sabalenka, she showed both facets of her game, bullying her from the baseline and digging in when necessary to leave her only a French Open title away from the career Grand Slam.

"Some magic is happening. I was unlucky with injury and just going day by day," Rybakina told Sky Sports.

"We didn't know how it was going to be so I'm super happy and still can't believe it."

The chance to beat the woman who had taken her number one ranking was extra motivation for Sabalenka.

However, it was evident from the early stages that the stress of the situation was still troubling the four-time major singles champion - and Rybakina's superb return of serve in the early exchanges only exacerbated it.

The pressure Sabalenka was feeling manifested in some aggressive second serves, and it was unsurprising to see one go long for a double fault on the decisive break point in the opening set.

While Sabalenka showed the resilience which she has demonstrated in her ascent to the top of the sport, she never looked completely at ease.

Dramatic displays of emotion designed to let off steam - yelling, flinging her arms in the air, bouncing her racquet off the court and hiding underneath her towel - were not enough to help produce a gutsy victory which would have ranked among her best.

Instead she will have to come to terms with another near miss at a Grand Slam.

It was Sabalenka's fifth defeat from nine majors final and provides further weight to the argument that she has underachieved at the biggest tournaments given her dominance on the WTA Tour.

"The last thing I want to do right now is give a speech but I will try my best," an emotional Sabalenka told the 24,000 crowd on Arthur Ashe Stadium.

"I wish I could have performed a little bit better, but I guess next year."

title: MSU defense show flaws without Jordan Hall, but return imminent
description: Jordan Hall missed Michigan State football's 35-7 win over Eastern Michigan with a right elbow injury, but he could play next week at Notre Dame.
fullText:
EAST LANSING — Michigan State coach Pat Fitzgerald thinks he may have his most important defensive player back for next week's game against Notre Dame.

In his postgame press conference after a 35-7 win over Eastern Michigan on Saturday, Sept. 12, Fitzgerald said that starting middle linebacker Jordan Hall was not cleared for the game by medical personnel but could be available for Week 3's rivalry game in South Bend.

"Jordan was really close playing today," Fitzgerald said. "Medical team told us that he was not cleared here late in the week. We made that decision collectively together to make sure that we think about his health, safety, and well-being. And I expect if we practice tomorrow that he'll be ready to go."

Hall made 88 tackles last season to lead Michigan State's defense and is a two-time captain. The senior made four tackles in 25 snaps in Week 1's win over Toledo but came on and off the field with a right elbow injury sustained on the second drive of the season. He walked into Spartan Stadium on Saturday with a brace on that right arm.

MSU LB Jordan Hall with a brace on his right elbow as he takes the Spartan Walk. 

Saw him wince on a couple of handshakes. We’ll see how he looks in warmups.@detroitnews pic.twitter.com/qklOKEfVbs

Without Hall, Michigan State leaned on linebacker Brady Pretzlaff to be its green dot — the player who communicates with defensive staff with helmet comms — and played a mix of Dion Crawford, Caleb Wheatland and Cam Stodghill next to him in a number of 4-2-5 and 4-3 looks. Fitzgerald said there is work for MSU's defense to do without Hall from a communication standpoint.

Pretzlaff credited Hall with preparing him to deliver on Saturday, when his eight tackles tied safety Devin Vaught for the team lead.

"I think Jordan himself has been a great leader throughout this week," Pretzlaff said. "It's hard for a guy like that who has played so much and is so passionate about the game to go down, and he's done a great job of himself kind of taking on the coaching role and getting us ready and kind of taking that role forward. So it's been great to see that, and I think our preparation really helped us attack it today."

More: Gaylord's Brady Pretzlaff proving MSU coaches' investment was worth it

The Spartans are 29-49-1 all-time against Notre Dame, which is ranked No. 4 in the USA Today Coaches Poll. In the past seven meetings dating back to 2009, Michigan State is 2-5 with an overtime win. Having Hall back will be important for Michigan State going into South Bend.

"Jordan's a huge piece of our program. He'll go down in Spartan lore when his career is said and done," Fitzgerald said. "So I don't want to minimize not having that big of a fixture of our defense out there, but it's next-man-up mentality, and those guys that went out there, I think learned a lot throughout the course of the game. I thought they played much better in the second half, and we need to continue to reinforce those guys playing that way."

Saturday, Sept. 19's game comes 60 years after Notre Dame ran out the clock against Michigan State in 1966's "Game of the Century," a 10-10 tie that led to both teams sharing pieces of the national championship that year.

Michigan State hasn't played Notre Dame since Sept. 23, 2017, when it lost 38-18 at Spartan Stadium.

title: Bay Area charity golf event raises $5.6 million for Curry's 'Eat. Learn. Play. Foundation'
description: The 7th Annual Workday Charity Classic at Palo Alto Hills Golf and Country Club raised more than $5.6 million dollars to support Oakland students and families.
fullText:
A perfect day on the golf course, resulted in a big win for Oakland children for many years to come. The 7th Annual Workday Charity Classic at Palo Alto Hills Golf and Country Club raised more than $5.6 million dollars to support Oakland students and families. The annual golf event is the signature fundraising event for the Curry's 'Eat. Learn. Play. Foundation.'

Seven years running, the @workday Charity Classic has turned a day on the green into real support for Oakland kids. This year’s event raised more than $5.6 million to support students, made possible in part by a generous matching gift from Aneel Bhusri, co-founder of Workday. pic.twitter.com/BijN8LaoIA

"This event is our biggest fundraiser of the year and the impact it helps us unlock in Oakland is huge," said Eat. Learn. Play. Foundation CEO Chris Helfrich. "To be able to pull together 150 of our best partners and supporters for a day full of joy and golf like this it's a big deal for 'Eat. Learn. Play.' and we are very fortunate to be able to raise the money and invest it back out so that kids in Oakland get what they deserve."

Related https://abc7news.com/post/golden-state-warriors-stephen-curry-surprises-minnesota-boy-viral-range-shot-invite-game-season/19229529/

MORE: 'Christmas with the Curry's' celebrates a decade of giving back to the community

The big donation was made possible in part by a generous matching gift from Aneel Bhursi, co-founder, CEO and Chari of Workday. Since 2019, nearly $15 million dollars have been raised to support Oakland Unified School District and Oakland youth and their families.

"It's been fantastic honestly because we work so hard on our mission and what we are trying to change within the community with these kids. So, when you actually start to see that come to fruition and you start to see the statistics change and these kids thriving in their environment, there is nothing better than that," said Eat. Learn. Play. Foundation co-founder Ayesha Curry.

Since the summer of 2019, 'Eat. Learn. Play. Foundation' has invested more than $100 million in Oakland students and families. The foundation's focus has been to bring resources to those who need it most and making sure the pillars of food (Eat), education (Learn) and activity (Play) are met.

Really wonderful conversation with Stephen and Ayesha Curry, along w/ Chris Helfrich on the growth of @eatlearnplay and the work ahead to continue investing in Oakland Unified School District and Bay Area youth. 

More to come soon on @abc7newsbayarea pic.twitter.com/jwQuETDWvj

"From the time we stepped foot out here back in 2009 before 'Eat. Learn. Play.' was even a thing you had an attachment to the community. You understood how much energy they give me on the court and following the journey," added Eat. Learn. Play. Foundation co-founder Stephen Curry. "So, now to be able to take that kind of relationship and hone it into what 'Eat. Learn. Play.' in the way it has been able to show up through the Oakland Unified School District, the ability to make sure they feel seen and loved and create resources that they can rely on to achieve their full potential. When we show up to the playground builds and activations we have, Christmas with the Curry's, those are highlights of the year."

Stephen Curry is now eligible for an extension and he tells me he's excited for year 18, "There's no secret I want to be here the rest of my career." @abc7newsbayarea @espn @ESPNNBA #DubNation #NBA pic.twitter.com/u6nRTLgSmq

MORE: Stephen, Ayesha Curry launch Eat. Learn. Play. Foundation to help underprivileged children in Bay Area

Since it's inception, the foundation has transformed 25 Oakland schoolyards and 6 gyms, and the work is just beginning.

"It's kind of gotten bigger than ourselves and more than we could have imagined, we are grateful. Any time we get a chance to be there and be present with the kids is very special," said Ayesha Curry.

title: Braves crush Phillies on big fourth inning
description: The Braves all-but locked up the NL East with a romp over the Phillies on Saturday night, as Tyler Mahle cruised
fullText:
After an epic 11-inning win Friday night against the Phillies, the Braves were hoping to finish them off in the division race. They got a bit of a boost from the Phillies scratching Jesus Luzardo with long-running shoulder soreness.

Tyler Mahle cruised through the first two hitters before Bryce Harper hit a monster homer and took a comical amount of time rounding the bases, clearly hitting back at the controversy from Zach Wheeler's comments about Ronald Acuna's home run celebrations last week. The Phillies had to be feeling good with a 1-0 lead for a couple innings there, until the Braves essentially ended the game with 8 runs in the fourth inning. Ronald Acuna kicked things off with a towering homer (and a normal home run trot).

La Bestia mode activated 🔥#LocalFordDealer | @ronaldacunajr24 pic.twitter.com/blKPAhoG0w

The Braves then got a walk, single, single, single, error, wild pitch, walk, double, and single to score another 7 runs. Drake Baldwin provided the double before things got all the way back around to Acuna for the last single, bringing home the last run of the inning.

Mahle continued to cruise after that Harper homer, finishing 7.0 innings of 1-run ball with no walks, even though he only had 7 whiffs and 3 strikeouts. The Braves added another run on in the sixth with a Ronald ABS strikeout-turned-walk, an error on an Olson ground ball, and an Ozzie sac fly. The Phillies got one back with a solo homer from Crawford in the eighth against Brent Suter. The Braves got another 3 runs against the position-player pitcher for Philly in the eighth, as Kiersey singled, Albies doubled, and Harris hit a homer off the right field foul pole. Suter finished off the Phillies in the ninth, as the Braves only needed to throw Mahle and Suter on the night. The Phillies' bullpen is in rough shape on the other side, after the 11-inning game Friday and the blowout bullpen game they suffered today.

Join us for hopefully the last time we see the Phillies this season tomorrow at 1:35 PM ET.

title: Woodland football answers offseason doubters with rout of GNH in coach Jeremy Clark's debut
description: Evan Mastropietro and a revamped Woodland lineup made an emphatic opening statement.
fullText:
WINSTED - New head coach, new starters, but not the same firepower as last year.

That's what the Woodland football team had been hearing during the offseason. The Hawks graduated a ton of seniors from a team that went 11-1 and reached the Class SS semifinals. Head coach Joe Lato resigned after the season, and Woodland alum Jeremy Clark was brought in.

On a beautiful Saturday afternoon at Van Why Field, Woodland got to show what it had and did so in a big way in a 56-7 season-opening win over GNH.

"All they wanted to prove was - hey, last year's team was great, now they just talk about how many guys we lost. They talk about this and that," Clark said. "Why don't we just go be ourselves and play for each other? That's how we've been playing ever since, so it's great."

Woodland ran for 324 yards and five touchdowns on 24 attempts, led by a game-high 128 yards and a touchdown from senior tight end-turned-quarterback Evan Mastropietro.

Senior guard-turned-fullback Colby Marsan ran six times for 46 yards and two scores, while senior wide receiver Justin Pringle carried three times for 33 yards and a score. Senior running back Daniel Keogh ran 73 yards for the game's final score in the fourth quarter and totaled 117 yards on six attempts.

Mastropietro was 6-of-11 passing for 96 yards and two touchdowns, one to senior Ryan Kenney (40 yards) and the other to Pringle (12 yards).

Senior kicker Hunter Cronk made all eight of his extra-point attempts.

"My coaches were telling me I'm going to be running a lot," said Mastropietro, who has always thought of himself as a defensive player. He is a linebacker on the Hawk defense.

"A lot of new starters out there, a lot of people probably weren't expecting us to come out as strong on offense as we did, and we didn't punt the ball one time," Pringle said. "We picked up where we left off on offense, keeping a good pace, and on defense, we made stops, so everything went pretty good."

Pringle added two interceptions on defense, including one he took back 63 yards for a touchdown.

Clark loved seeing Marsan live out every big man's dream to run the football. Mastropietro shifted from being "an unbelievable tight end" to quarterback. Pringle went from cornerback to safety.

"It's something they've embraced, and they've become leaders in that position," Clark said.

Junior Airyn Berube went 57 yards on an option pitch for the lone GNH touchdown, and Daniel Nolan made the extra point.

The touchdown got the Yellowjackets to within 28-7, but the Hawks immediately answered with their own touchdown and ran away with the game.

GNH has 30 players on its roster, and many were learning how to be varsity players on the fly during the preseason.

"A pick-six right off in the second series, that hurt. Then a botched kickoff where we gave the ball right to them," GNH coach Scott Salius said. "You can't do that against teams like Woodland. You can't give them opportunities like this.

"Especially if we're going to have to scrap for wins, to give them six points and then give a kickoff right back to them? The underdog can't really come back from those mistakes too well."

The senior quarterback ran nine times for 128 yards, threw for 96 yards, and was part of three touchdowns in his team's victory.

"When you get a lot of texts in the morning talking to people in the community, and living in the community, you feel the pressure right away," Clark said. "We had a pep rally the other week, full of the town, and I was like 'Oh boy, it's real now.' It's been a cool environment, but also the pressure's great. I love it and I embrace it. Coming from here, it's great." - Woodland coach Jeremy Clark on the run-up to his first game

title: DNSCrypt
fullText:
DNSCrypt is a network protocol that authenticates and encrypts Domain Name System (DNS) traffic between the user's computer and recursive name servers. DNSCrypt wraps unmodified DNS traffic between a client and a DNS resolver in a cryptographic construction, preventing eavesdropping and forgery by a man-in-the-middle.[1]

It also mitigates UDP-based amplification attacks by requiring a question to be at least as large as the corresponding response. Thus, DNSCrypt helps to prevent DNS amplification attacks.[2]: §9

DNSCrypt was originally designed by Frank Denis and Yecheng Fu. Multiple free and open source software implementations exist. It is available for a variety of operating systems, including Unix, Apple iOS, Linux, Android, and Microsoft Windows.[3] The free and open source software implementation dnscrypt-proxy[4] additionally integrates ODoH.[5]

In addition to private deployments, the DNSCrypt protocol has been adopted by several public DNS resolvers, the vast majority being members of the OpenNIC network, as well as virtual private network (VPN) services.

OpenDNS (now a part of Cisco) announced the first public DNS service supporting DNSCrypt on 6 December 2011, shortly followed by CloudNS Australia.[6]

On 29 March 2016, Yandex announced support for the DNSCrypt protocol on their public DNS servers, as well as in Yandex Browser.[citation needed]

On 14 October 2016, AdGuard added DNSCrypt to their DNS filtering module so that users could move from their ISPs to custom or AdGuard's own DNS servers for online privacy and ad blocking.[7][8]

On 10 September 2018, the Quad9 nonprofit public recursive resolver service announced support for DNSCrypt.[9]

Other servers that support secure protocol are mentioned in the DNSCrypt creators' list.[10]

DNSCrypt can be used either over UDP or over TCP. In both cases, its default port is 443.[2] Even though the protocol radically differs from HTTPS, both service types utilize the same port. However, even though DNS over HTTPS and DNSCrypt are possible on the same port, they must still run separately on different servers. Two server applications cannot run simultaneously on the same server if both utilize the same port for communication; though a multiplexing approach is theoretically possible.

Instead of relying on trusted certificate authorities commonly found in web browsers, the client has to explicitly trust the public signing key of the chosen provider. This public key is used to verify a set of certificates, retrieved using conventional DNS queries.[2]: §1  These certificates contain short-term public keys used for key exchange, as well as an identifier of the cipher suite to use. Clients are encouraged to generate a new key for every query, while servers are encouraged to rotate short-term key pairs every 24 hours.[2]: §13

The DNSCrypt protocol can also be used for access control or accounting, by accepting only a predefined set of public keys. This can be used by commercial DNS services to identify customers without having to rely on IP addresses.[2]: §13

Queries and responses are encrypted using the same algorithm and padded to a multiple of 64 bytes in order to avoid leaking packet sizes. Over UDP, when a response would be larger than the question leading to it, a server can respond with a short packet whose TC (truncated) bit has been set. The client should then retry using TCP and increase the padding of subsequent queries.[2]: §9

Versions 1 and 2 of the protocol use the X25519 algorithm for key exchange, EdDSA for signatures, as well as XSalsa20-Poly1305 or XChaCha20-Poly1305 for authenticated encryption.[2]: §11

As of 2023, there are no known vulnerabilities in the DNSCrypt protocol nor practical attacks against its underlying cryptographic constructions.

Anonymized DNSCrypt is a protocol extension proposed in 2019 to further improve DNS privacy.[11]

Instead of directly responding to clients, a resolver can act as a transparent proxy to another resolver, hiding the real client IP to the latter. Anonymized DNSCrypt, specifically designed for DNS traffic, is a lightweight alternative to running DNSCrypt through Tor and SOCKS proxies.[11]

Deployment of Anonymized DNSCrypt started in October 2019, and the protocol adoption was fast, with 40 DNS relays being set up only two weeks after the public availability of client and server implementations.[12]

title: Align AI and Mathematics–To Something Else
description: Twenty five Fields medalists were initial signatories of the letter “A Severe Misalignment of AI in Mathematics” in which they opine that “The goals of the AI companies and the go…
fullText:
Twenty five Fields medalists were initial signatories of the letter “A Severe Misalignment of AI in Mathematics” in which they opine that “The goals of the AI companies and the goals of the mathematical community are severely misaligned”. They are right.

As they say, the goals of AI companies do not seem to be aligned with “the primary goal of conceptual understanding and insight”, and indeed, the “solutions [by AI companies] are [being] announced in a rush, leaving no time for a proper writeup, the isolation of new methods and ideas, and citing relevant previous work of others.” This is true (but ironically, the signatories themselves say they released their letter quickly because they “did not have the time to have a more consultative process.”)

It is also true that the goals of the mathematics community do not seem to be aligned with “the primary goal of conceptual understanding and insight”. This is clear, because if that were the goal, then the mathematics community would hold the view that “the most precious resources of [its] profession are students and ideas”, and that they would be “nurture[d] with great care”. But sadly students and ideas in mathematics have not been nurtured with great care.

Since the letter by the twenty five Fields medalists seems to have been precipitated by the OpenAI announcement a solution to the Navier Stokes existence and smoothness problem, let’s take a look at how the mathematics community has nurtured some of the students who worked in that area, and their foundational ideas.

Of course every mathematician knows that the mathematics community does not nurture with great care all of its students and ideas. This is not a secret and it’s not an open secret. It’s just common knowledge. In the mathematics department at UC Berkeley, where I worked for 18 years, the department went from barring Julia Robinson (Hilbert’s tenth problem) from teaching mathematics for 35 years (also using the nepotism rule as an excuse and agreeing to appoint her only after she was elected to the National Academy of Sciences in 1976) to hiring Yuval Peres (Berkeley math professor ~2001 – 2011). A particularly shocking detail about Robinson is that she was required to document to the personnel office exactly what she worked on every single day (!) In Peres’ case eventually mathematicians publicly described at least seven cases or reports involving junior women, some of whom reportedly avoided conferences or lectures to escape his repeated advances. It was not surprising to me that just three years after I arrived at the UC Berkeley math department, the department lost an important NSF grant specifically due to poor student mentorship. And it’s outrageous that there is still a prominent faculty member at UC Berkeley (now emeritus) who even today insists there is no, and never has been, sexism in mathematics.

One of the defining moments for me in the department was when a graduate student who I knew only in passing, came to my office in tears to tell me “I’ve just been told I’m stupid” (she is now a very successful professor of mathematics). I’d heard this insult made many times in the department. Once at a faculty meeting a senior professor was asked what he was doing to help one of his graduate students who was in his 9th or 10th year. The reply was “I’m doing nothing. He’s stupid”. These are not isolated anecdotes. Many mathematicians have experienced rejection not only of their ideas, but of themselves. Perhaps one of the most egregious examples is Yitang Zhang who was told by his advisor “no Chinese student is good“. Was this “nurture with great care”?

I found it interesting that the 25 primary signatories on the “A Severe Misalignment of AI in Mathematics” signed the letter with “Fields medalist” in parenthesis. Why not their affiliation, or email address? Did they highlight that they are Fields medal winners to imply that the honor bestows upon them some kind of authority on the mathematics community? Sure- they all did some incredibly important mathematics and were recognized based on extraordinary mathematical ability. But receipt of a Fields Medal also depends on the judgments of a tiny group about which problems, fields, and styles of mathematics deserve recognition. Erdős remarked that “Szemerédi should have gotten a Fields Medal. [But] the people who decide are not that interested in combinatorics.” Indeed, prizes encode judgments about which mathematics, and therefore which mathematicians, matter. But regardless of Fields medal politics, the point is that mathematical ability is not the same as mathematical responsibility. Perhaps instead of foregrounding Fields medalists in a letter about “alignment,” it would have been more illuminating to hear from mathematicians whose careers were derailed by lack of mentorship and nurturing.

So yes, there is severe misalignment of AI in mathematics. But alignment of AI with the existing mathematics community should not be the goal. The history of mathematics gives us little reason to treat the profession’s existing incentives, hierarchies, and institutions as a model. AI companies and mathematicians should instead be asking what both ought to be aligned to: understanding, attribution, intellectual generosity, and the nurturing of students and ideas, and not merely the production or recognition of results.

It’s crucial to get medical treatment right away. Getting emergency medical help quickly can reduce brain damage and other stroke complications.

A stroke is a medical emergency that occurs when blood flow to a part of the brain is interrupted, either by a blockage (ischemic stroke) or by bleeding (hemorrhagic stroke). When brain cells are deprived of oxygen-rich blood, they begin to die within minutes, making immediate medical attention critical.

Strokes are one of the leading causes of death and disability in the United States, but the good news is that most strokes are both preventable and treatable, especially when recognized early and responded to quickly.

The chances of recovery improve greatly when a stroke is recognized and treated as soon as symptoms begin. Unfortunately, many people do not realize when they or someone else is experiencing a stroke. That’s why understanding the signs and symptoms is essential.

A simple way to remember the signs of a stroke is the acronym BE FAST Each letter stands for a common symptom that may appear suddenly:

Every second counts. The sooner a stroke is treated, the better the chances of minimizing long-term damage.

Up to 80% of strokes can be prevented by managing common risk factors. Here are a few ways to reduce your risk:

Whether you’re managing your own health or watching out for a loved one, knowing the warning signs of stroke and acting quickly can be life-saving. If something feels off, trust your instincts and seek emergency medical help.

title: Apple wants to train AI on your private personal data
description: Our next generation of Apple Intelligence is centered around our users, integrated deeply into our operating systems, and powered by a bold…
fullText:
Introducing the Third Generation of Apple’s Foundation Models

Our next generation of Apple Intelligence is centered around our users, integrated deeply into our operating systems, and powered by a bold new architecture with privacy at its core.

At the heart of this architecture is our third generation of Apple Foundation Models (AFM), a family of five foundation models custom-built in collaboration with Google. These span from on-device models to server-based models running on Private Cloud Compute.

Apple Foundation Models are built to unlock a wide range of helpful experiences for our users, like an entirely new Siri and intelligent tools that make everyday apps smarter and more useful.

This family of models includes two on-device models:

Our latest Apple Foundation Models also include three server-based models running on Private Cloud Compute, which ensures that user data is never stored or shared with anyone, including Apple. These models are:

AFM 3 Core, AFM 3 Core Advanced, and AFM 3 Cloud, along with ADM 3 Cloud, are all purpose-built for Apple silicon.

For AFM 3 Cloud Pro, we worked with Google and NVIDIA to extend Private Cloud Compute to NVIDIA GPUs in Google Cloud, while maintaining the same guarantees to protect our users’ privacy. More details are available on our Security Research Website.

Our third generation of Apple Foundation Models delivers significant advancements across capabilities and quality. In the following overview, we’ll dive deeper to explore the scalable architectures powering our on-device and server-based models, our training methodologies, and more.

We designed the architectures for both our on-device and server-side models to enable powerful Apple Intelligence experiences for our users, and we integrated our latest models deep into our operating systems.

One area of deep innovation is our most powerful on-device model, AFM 3 Core Advanced. Traditional large language models—whether dense or sparsely activated—require all weights to reside in active memory (DRAM), creating a massive footprint that limits scalability on consumer hardware. To break this barrier, AFM 3 Core Advanced introduces a novel sparsely activated architecture built on Instruction-Following Pruning (IFP), a technique developed by Apple researchers (see Figure 1).

Instead of forcing the entire model into DRAM, the full model is stored in flash memory (NAND). Because NAND-to-DRAM bandwidth is too slow to swap weights token by token, as standard MoE models require, AFM 3 Core Advanced makes routing decisions per prompt. A lightweight, dense block selects a fixed set of experts during initial processing, periodically reselecting them during generation. To minimize data movement, the model relies on a high percentage of always-active “shared experts” alongside input-dependent “routed experts” swapped into DRAM only when needed.

This design also introduces crucial inference-time elasticity. Rather than using a single model for all tasks or managing an ensemble of smaller models, AFM 3 Core Advanced uses a predetermined number of active parameters tailored to each specific use case. This allows weights to be loaded incrementally across requests of varying difficulty, scaling the model size far beyond traditional DRAM limits while minimizing latency.

In addition to innovation across on-device AI, we’re also taking a big step forward for our server-based models. For instance, our server-side model, AFM 3 Cloud, represents a substantial step forward in multimodal reasoning powered by Private Cloud Compute. To achieve this, we implemented several key upgrades to the Parallel-Track Mixture-of-Experts (PT-MoE) foundation we introduced last year. These architectural refinements stabilize training and improve the model’s ability to reason over and accurately recall information within its context window for complex server-side queries.

Another example where we advanced our model architecture is our latest image model, ADM 3 Cloud. To power high-quality image creation (see Figure 2), editing, and Genmoji, we developed ADM 3 Cloud to deliver strong controllability and parameter efficiency. It generalizes across different aspect ratios and resolutions, and draws on the broader Apple Foundation Model family to guide both creation and editing. While the base model natively handles image creation, editing, and Genmoji, we also use specialized adapters to power specific downstream editing experiences, such as Spatial Reframing in Photos, along with touch-based image modifications and personalization in Image Playground.

Capable foundation models require diverse, high-quality data. To train our foundation models, we use a mixture of data that includes publicly available information, data licensed or purchased from third parties, open-sourced data, data obtained through dedicated studies, and synthetic data. We do not use our users’ private personal data or user interactions when training our foundation models. We also respect the rights of web publishers to opt out of foundation model training.

To support our new Apple Intelligence experiences, we significantly scaled pre-training on the latest generation of cloud TPU accelerators. All models shared a common initial foundation before specializing for their respective architectures and use cases, adding multimodal capabilities like audio, image understanding, long-context reasoning, and high-quality visual generation. We then expanded our post-training process, combining supervised fine-tuning with multi-stage reinforcement learning.

Finally, we optimized each model for its target hardware. AFM 3 Core, AFM 3 Core Advanced, AFM 3 Cloud, and ADM 3 Cloud (Image) were optimized to run efficiently on Apple silicon, while AFM 3 Cloud Pro was optimized for NVIDIA GPUs. Using Quantization Aware Training, we compressed our models substantially while maintaining high accuracy, together delivering the responsive, high-quality experiences our users expect.

Our third-generation Apple Foundation Models are designed to power integrated Apple Intelligence experiences that make our operating systems smarter and more helpful, and we conduct quality evaluations at both the model and feature levels.

Below, we detail our model-level evaluations first, followed by results for features unlocked by our models. These evaluations reflect our models at their current stage of development. During the beta period, we’ll continue improving them to deliver great experiences for our users.

To ensure an exceptional experience, in-house human graders assess model responses along key dimensions, including Instruction Following, Truthfulness, and Presentation. For image-based prompts, we also evaluate Image Understanding, measuring the model’s ability to successfully identify, extract, and reason about visual content.

Across these dimensions, our on-device models demonstrate substantial generational progress. For general text capabilities, the updated AFM 3 Core model improved upon its predecessor, earning preference on 45.6 percent of prompts compared to 23.3 percent for the 2025 baseline (see Figure 3). This progress extends to visual inputs; for image understanding, in cases where users preferred one over the other, they preferred AFM 3 Core over the previous generation more than 61 percent of the time (see Figure 4).

Our server model, AFM 3 Cloud, also significantly improved upon its predecessor. In side-by-side human evaluations for general text capabilities, it was preferred on 64.7 percent of prompts compared to only 8.7 percent for the 2025 AFM Server model, a generational leap consistent across all locale regions. We also see consistent gains in our single-sided evaluations, which score responses independently along multiple dimensions: AFM 3 Cloud delivers a roughly 36 percent relative improvement in overall response satisfaction and a 21 percent relative improvement in instruction following performance over the 2025 AFM Server model. Further, for image understanding, where the model interprets and reasons over visual inputs, AFM 3 Cloud showed significant improvement over its predecessor from last year, earning preference on 37.8 percent of prompts compared to just 9.6 percent for its 2025 baseline.

Finally, AFM 3 Cloud Pro provides an even further improvement over our AFM 3 Cloud, achieving a relative improvement in overall response satisfaction of roughly 10 percent for text and 14 percent for image understanding overall. AFM 3 Cloud Pro excels in specific task categories such as Math, showing a relative 14 percent improvement over AFM 3 Cloud.

Beyond model-level evaluation, we also evaluate all of the features powered by our foundation models. Below, we highlight a few of these results.

To measure the quality of our new expressive voices, human evaluators graded AFM 3 Core Advanced against Apple’s existing production Text-to-Speech (TTS) system using a 5-point Mean Opinion Score (MOS) scale (see Table 1). Operating at its efficient 1-billion-parameter activation size, AFM 3 Core Advanced achieved an overall score of 4.15—a strong 0.28 increase over the current production baseline, especially given that a 0.1 increase on the MOS scale represents a highly noticeable improvement in the customer experience (see Audio 1). This quality gap widens even further on conversational text, like the casual language used when reading a text aloud. In these conversational scenarios, AFM 3 Core Advanced scored 4.24 compared to the production system’s 3.82, an even larger 0.42 delta that demonstrates a significantly more natural and expressive audio experience.

Complementing these text-to-speech improvements, AFM 3 Core Advanced demonstrates significant progress in its speech-to-text capabilities (see Figure 5). For specific downstream features like dictation, we collected side-by-side preference judgments against our previous dictation system along seven dimensions: Overall Quality, Punctuation, Casing, Layout, Meaning Capture, Disfluency Handling, and Style. At its 1-billion-parameter activation size, AFM 3 Core Advanced is preferred on Overall Quality by a margin of 44.7 percent to 17.6 percent, and this preference extends consistently across each of the six remaining dimensions.

Our latest Apple Foundation Models are designed with our core values at every step and built on a foundation of industry-leading privacy protection. Additionally, at every stage of developing and advancing Apple Intelligence and Apple Foundation Models, we use our Responsible AI principles to guide our features and models:

Our safety taxonomy helps us identify sensitive content that should be handled with care. To ensure our models respect these boundaries across linguistic and cultural contexts, we conduct multilingual post-training alignment, use language-specific guardrail models, and conduct human red teaming refined by native speakers across our supported locales. We are continuously working to improve our models’ alignment with our Responsible AI approach, and our latest models show significant progress.

Our third generation of Apple Foundation Models represents a big step forward, powering new Apple Intelligence experiences that make our operating systems even more helpful for our users. This includes an entirely new version of Siri, advanced photo-editing tools, powerful updates to Image Playground, incredibly expressive voices, and more. To protect our users’ privacy, these models run exclusively on-device and on Private Cloud Compute. We look forward to sharing more details on our latest foundation models, including updated evaluations and benchmarks, in a technical report later this summer.
